Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.SuppressDocWarningsGuard.level(JSError)

51 |   @Override
52 |   public CheckLevel level(JSError error) {
53 |     Node node = error.node;
54 |     if (node != null) {
55 |       for (Node current = node;
56 |            current != null;
57 |            current = current.getParent()) {
58 |         int type = current.getType();
59 |         JSDocInfo info = null;
60 | 
61 |         // We only care about function annotations at the FUNCTION and SCRIPT
62 |         // level. Otherwise, the @suppress annotation has an implicit
63 |         // dependency on the exact structure of our AST, and that seems like
64 |         // a bad idea.
65 |         if (type == Token.FUNCTION) {
66 |           info = NodeUtil.getFunctionJSDocInfo(current);
67 |         } else if (type == Token.SCRIPT) {
68 |           info = current.getJSDocInfo();
69 |         } else if (type == Token.ASSIGN) {
70 |           Node rhs = current.getLastChild();
71 |           if (rhs.isFunction()) {
72 |             info = NodeUtil.getFunctionJSDocInfo(rhs);
73 |           }
74 |         }
75 | 
76 |         if (info != null) {
77 |           for (String suppressor : info.getSuppressions()) {
78 |             WarningsGuard guard = suppressors.get(suppressor);
79 | 
80 |             // Some @suppress tags are for other tools, and
81 |             // may not have a warnings guard.
82 |             if (guard != null) {
83 |               CheckLevel newLevel = guard.level(error);
84 |               if (newLevel != null) {
85 |                 return newLevel;
86 |               }
87 |             }
88 |           }
89 |         }
90 |       }
91 |     }
92 |     return null;
93 |   }

===== M0013 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Normalize.NormalizeStatements.extractForInitializer(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Normalize.java
Original range: 560-607
Documentation:
/**
     * Bring the initializers out of FOR loops.  These need to be placed
     * before any associated LABEL nodes. This needs to be done from the top
     * level label first so this is called as a pre-order callback (from
     * shouldTraverse).
     *
     * @param n The node to inspect.
     * @param before The node to insert the initializer before.
     * @param beforeParent The parent of the node before which the initializer
     *     will be inserted.
     */
Method code:
560 |     private void extractForInitializer(
561 |         Node n, Node before, Node beforeParent) {
562 | 
563 |       for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
564 |         next = c.getNext();
565 |         Node insertBefore = (before == null) ? c : before;
566 |         Node insertBeforeParent = (before == null) ? n : beforeParent;
567 |         switch (c.getType()) {
568 |           case Token.LABEL:
569 |             extractForInitializer(c, insertBefore, insertBeforeParent);
570 |             break;
571 |           case Token.FOR:
572 |             if (NodeUtil.isForIn(c)) {
573 |               Node first = c.getFirstChild();
574 |               if (first.isVar()) {
575 |                 // Transform:
576 |                 //    for (var a = 1 in b) {}
577 |                 // to:
578 |                 //    var a = 1; for (a in b) {};
579 |                 Node newStatement = first;
580 |                 // Clone just the node, to remove any initialization.
581 |                 Node name = newStatement.getFirstChild().cloneNode();
582 |                 first.getParent().replaceChild(first, name);
583 |                 insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
584 |                 reportCodeChange("FOR-IN var declaration");
585 |               }
586 |             } else if (!c.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
587 |               Node init = c.getFirstChild();
588 |               Node empty = IR.empty();
589 |               empty.copyInformationFrom(c);
590 |               c.replaceChild(init, empty);
591 | 
592 |               Node newStatement;
593 |               // Only VAR statements, and expressions are allowed,
594 |               // but are handled differently.
595 |               if (init.isVar()) {
596 |                 newStatement = init;
597 |               } else {
598 |                 newStatement = NodeUtil.newExpr(init);
599 |               }
600 | 
601 |               insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
602 |               reportCodeChange("FOR initializer");
603 |             }
604 |             break;
605 |         }
606 |       }
607 |     }

===== M0019 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocInfoParser.java
Original range: 1686-1727
Documentation:
/**
   * TypeExpression := BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '?' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '!' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '?'
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '!'
   *     | '?'
   */
Method code:
1686 |   private Node parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {
1687 |     if (token == JsDocToken.QMARK) {
1688 |       // A QMARK could mean that a type is nullable, or that it's unknown.
1689 |       // We use look-ahead 1 to determine whether it's unknown. Otherwise,
1690 |       // we assume it means nullable. There are 5 cases:
1691 |       // {?} - right curly
1692 |       // {?=} - equals
1693 |       // {function(?, number)} - comma
1694 |       // {function(number, ?)} - right paren
1695 |       // {function(number, ...[?])} - right bracket
1696 |       // {function(): ?|number} - pipe
1697 |       // I'm not a big fan of using look-ahead for this, but it makes
1698 |       // the type language a lot nicer.
1699 |       token = next();
1700 |       if (token == JsDocToken.COMMA ||
1701 |           token == JsDocToken.EQUALS ||
1702 |           token == JsDocToken.RB ||
1703 |           token == JsDocToken.RC ||
1704 |           token == JsDocToken.RP ||
1705 |           token == JsDocToken.PIPE) {
1706 |         restoreLookAhead(token);
1707 |         return newNode(Token.QMARK);
1708 |       }
1709 | 
1710 |       return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, parseBasicTypeExpression(token));
1711 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.BANG) {
1712 |       return wrapNode(Token.BANG, parseBasicTypeExpression(next()));
1713 |     } else {
1714 |       Node basicTypeExpr = parseBasicTypeExpression(token);
1715 |       if (basicTypeExpr != null) {
1716 |         if (match(JsDocToken.QMARK)) {
1717 |           next();
1718 |           return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, basicTypeExpr);
1719 |         } else if (match(JsDocToken.BANG)) {
1720 |           next();
1721 |           return wrapNode(Token.BANG, basicTypeExpr);
1722 |         }
1723 |       }
1724 | 
1725 |       return basicTypeExpr;
1726 |     }
1727 |   }

===== M0058 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(Node,Node,ControlFlowAnalysis)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 692-789
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the follow() node of a given node and its parent. There is a side
   * effect when calling this function. If this function computed an edge that
   * exists a FINALLY, it'll attempt to connect the fromNode to the outer
   * FINALLY according to the finallyMap.
   *
   * @param fromNode The original source node since {@code node} is changed
   *        during recursion.
   * @param node The node that follow() should compute.
   */
Method code:
692 |   private static Node computeFollowNode(
693 |       Node fromNode, Node node, ControlFlowAnalysis cfa) {
694 |     /*
695 |      * This is the case where:
696 |      *
697 |      * 1. Parent is null implies that we are transferring control to the end of
698 |      * the script.
699 |      *
700 |      * 2. Parent is a function implies that we are transferring control back to
701 |      * the caller of the function.
702 |      *
703 |      * 3. If the node is a return statement, we should also transfer control
704 |      * back to the caller of the function.
705 |      *
706 |      * 4. If the node is root then we have reached the end of what we have been
707 |      * asked to traverse.
708 |      *
709 |      * In all cases we should transfer control to a "symbolic return" node.
710 |      * This will make life easier for DFAs.
711 |      */
712 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
713 |     if (parent == null || parent.isFunction() ||
714 |         (cfa != null && node == cfa.root)) {
715 |       return null;
716 |     }
717 | 
718 |     // If we are just before a IF/WHILE/DO/FOR:
719 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
720 |       // The follow() of any of the path from IF would be what follows IF.
721 |       case Token.IF:
722 |         return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
723 |       case Token.CASE:
724 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
725 |         // After the body of a CASE, the control goes to the body of the next
726 |         // case, without having to go to the case condition.
727 |         if (parent.getNext() != null) {
728 |           if (parent.getNext().isCase()) {
729 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild().getNext();
730 |           } else if (parent.getNext().isDefaultCase()) {
731 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild();
732 |           } else {
733 |             Preconditions.checkState(false, "Not reachable");
734 |           }
735 |         } else {
736 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
737 |         }
738 |         break;
739 |       case Token.FOR:
740 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
741 |           return parent;
742 |         } else {
743 |           return parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
744 |         }
745 |       case Token.WHILE:
746 |       case Token.DO:
747 |         return parent;
748 |       case Token.TRY:
749 |         // If we are coming out of the TRY block...
750 |         if (parent.getFirstChild() == node) {
751 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
752 |             return computeFallThrough(parent.getLastChild());
753 |           } else { // and have no FINALLY.
754 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
755 |           }
756 |         // CATCH block.
757 |         } else if (NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node){
758 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
759 |             return computeFallThrough(node.getNext());
760 |           } else {
761 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
762 |           }
763 |         // If we are coming out of the FINALLY block...
764 |         } else if (parent.getLastChild() == node){
765 |           if (cfa != null) {
766 |             for (Node finallyNode : cfa.finallyMap.get(parent)) {
767 |               cfa.createEdge(fromNode, Branch.UNCOND, finallyNode);
768 |             }
769 |           }
770 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
771 |         }
772 |     }
773 | 
774 |     // Now that we are done with the special cases follow should be its
775 |     // immediate sibling, unless its sibling is a function
776 |     Node nextSibling = node.getNext();
777 | 
778 |     // Skip function declarations because control doesn't get pass into it.
779 |     while (nextSibling != null && nextSibling.isFunction()) {
780 |       nextSibling = nextSibling.getNext();
781 |     }
782 | 
783 |     if (nextSibling != null) {
784 |       return computeFallThrough(nextSibling);
785 |     } else {
786 |       // If there are no more siblings, control is transferred up the AST.
787 |       return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
788 |     }
789 |   }

===== M0069 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.PhaseOptimizer.consume(List<PassFactory>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PhaseOptimizer.java
Original range: 125-146
Documentation:
/**
   * Add the passes generated by the given factories to the compile sequence.
   *
   * Automatically pulls multi-run passes into fixed point loops. If there
   * are 2 or more multi-run passes in a row, they will run together in
   * the same fixed point loop. If A and B are in the same fixed point loop,
   * the loop will continue to run both A and B until both are finished
   * making changes.
   *
   * Other than that, the PhaseOptimizer is free to tweak the order and
   * frequency of multi-run passes in a fixed-point loop.
   */
Method code:
125 |   void consume(List<PassFactory> factories) {
126 |     Loop currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
127 |     boolean isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
128 |     for (PassFactory factory : factories) {
129 |       if (factory.isOneTimePass()) {
130 |         if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
131 |           passes.add(currentLoop);
132 | 
133 |           currentLoop = new LoopInternal();
134 |           isCurrentLoopPopulated = false;
135 |         }
136 |         addOneTimePass(factory);
137 |       } else {
138 |         currentLoop.addLoopedPass(factory);
139 |         isCurrentLoopPopulated = true;
140 |       }
141 |     }
142 | 
143 |     if (isCurrentLoopPopulated) {
144 |       passes.add(currentLoop);
145 |     }
146 |   }

/**
   * Updates the scope according to the result of a type change, like
   * an assignment or a type cast.
   */
Method code:
462 |   private void updateScopeForTypeChange(
463 |       FlowScope scope, Node left, JSType leftType, JSType resultType) {
464 |     Preconditions.checkNotNull(resultType);
465 |     switch (left.getType()) {
466 |       case Token.NAME:
467 |         String varName = left.getString();
468 |         Var var = syntacticScope.getVar(varName);
469 | 
470 |         // When looking at VAR initializers for declared VARs, we trust
471 |         // the declared type over the type it's being initialized to.
472 |         // This has two purposes:
473 |         // 1) We avoid re-declaring declared variables so that built-in
474 |         //    types defined in externs are not redeclared.
475 |         // 2) When there's a lexical closure like
476 |         //    /** @type {?string} */ var x = null;
477 |         //    function f() { x = 'xyz'; }
478 |         //    the inference will ignore the lexical closure,
479 |         //    which is just wrong. This bug needs to be fixed eventually.
480 |         boolean isVarDeclaration = left.hasChildren();
481 |         if (!isVarDeclaration || var == null || var.isTypeInferred()) {
482 |           redeclareSimpleVar(scope, left, resultType);
483 |         }
484 |         left.setJSType(isVarDeclaration || leftType == null ?
485 |             resultType : null);
486 | 
487 |         if (var != null && var.isTypeInferred()) {
488 |           JSType oldType = var.getType();
489 |           var.setType(oldType == null ?
490 |               resultType : oldType.getLeastSupertype(resultType));
491 |         }
492 |         break;
493 |       case Token.GETPROP:
494 |         String qualifiedName = left.getQualifiedName();
495 |         if (qualifiedName != null) {
496 |           scope.inferQualifiedSlot(left, qualifiedName,
497 |               leftType == null ? getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE) : leftType,
498 |               resultType);

===== M0079 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Denormalize.maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Denormalize.java
Original range: 65-127
Documentation:
/**
   * Collapse VARs and EXPR_RESULT node into FOR loop initializers where
   * possible.
   */
Method code:
65 |   private void maybeCollapseIntoForStatements(Node n, Node parent) {
66 |     // Only SCRIPT, BLOCK, and LABELs can have FORs that can be collapsed into.
67 |     // LABELs are not supported here.
68 |     if (parent == null || !NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(parent)) {
69 |       return;
70 |     }
71 | 
72 |     // Is the current node something that can be in a for loop initializer?
73 |     if (!n.isExprResult() && !n.isVar()) {
74 |       return;
75 |     }
76 | 
77 |     // Is the next statement a valid FOR?
78 |     Node nextSibling = n.getNext();
79 |     if (nextSibling == null) {
80 |       return;
81 |     } else if (NodeUtil.isForIn(nextSibling)) {
82 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
83 |       Node forVar = forNode.getFirstChild();
84 |       if (forVar.isName()
85 |           && n.isVar() && n.hasOneChild()) {
86 |         Node name = n.getFirstChild();
87 |         if (!name.hasChildren()
88 |             && forVar.getString().equals(name.getString())) {
89 |           // OK, the names match, and the var declaration does not have an
90 |           // initializer. Move it into the loop.
91 |           parent.removeChild(n);
92 |           forNode.replaceChild(forVar, n);
93 |           compiler.reportCodeChange();
94 |         }
95 |       }
96 |     } else if (nextSibling.isFor()
97 |         && nextSibling.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
98 | 
99 |       // Does the current node contain an in operator?  If so, embedding
100 |       // the expression in a for loop can cause some JavaScript parsers (such
101 |       // as the PlayStation 3's browser based on Access's NetFront
102 |       // browser) to fail to parse the code.
103 |       // See bug 1778863 for details.
104 |       if (NodeUtil.containsType(n, Token.IN)) {
105 |         return;
106 |       }
107 | 
108 |       // Move the current node into the FOR loop initializer.
109 |       Node forNode = nextSibling;
110 |       Node oldInitializer = forNode.getFirstChild();
111 |       parent.removeChild(n);
112 | 
113 |       Node newInitializer;
114 |       if (n.isVar()) {
115 |         newInitializer = n;
116 |       } else {
117 |         // Extract the expression from EXPR_RESULT node.
118 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.hasOneChild());
119 |         newInitializer = n.getFirstChild();
120 |         n.removeChild(newInitializer);
121 |       }
122 | 
123 |       forNode.replaceChild(oldInitializer, newInitializer);
124 | 
125 |       compiler.reportCodeChange();
126 |     }
127 |   }

===== M0089 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.FunctionTypeBuilder.buildAndRegister()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/FunctionTypeBuilder.java
Original range: 576-638
Documentation:
/**
   * Builds the function type, and puts it in the registry.
   */
Method code:
576 |   FunctionType buildAndRegister() {
577 |     if (returnType == null) {
578 |       // Infer return types.
579 |       // We need to be extremely conservative about this, because of two
580 |       // competing needs.
581 |       // 1) If we infer the return type of f too widely, then we won't be able
582 |       //    to assign f to other functions.
583 |       // 2) If we infer the return type of f too narrowly, then we won't be
584 |       //    able to override f in subclasses.
585 |       // So we only infer in cases where the user doesn't expect to write
586 |       // @return annotations--when it's very obvious that the function returns
587 |       // nothing.
588 |       if (!contents.mayHaveNonEmptyReturns() &&
589 |           !contents.mayHaveSingleThrow() &&
590 |           !contents.mayBeFromExterns()) {
591 |         returnType = typeRegistry.getNativeType(VOID_TYPE);
592 |         returnTypeInferred = true;
593 |       }
594 |     }
595 | 
596 |     if (returnType == null) {
597 |       returnType = typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE);
598 |     }
599 | 
600 |     if (parametersNode == null) {
601 |       throw new IllegalStateException(
602 |           "All Function types must have params and a return type");
603 |     }
604 | 
605 |     FunctionType fnType;
606 |     if (isConstructor) {
607 |       fnType = getOrCreateConstructor();
608 |     } else if (isInterface) {
609 |       fnType = typeRegistry.createInterfaceType(
610 |           fnName, contents.getSourceNode());
611 |       if (getScopeDeclaredIn().isGlobal() && !fnName.isEmpty()) {
612 |         typeRegistry.declareType(fnName, fnType.getInstanceType());
613 |       }
614 |       maybeSetBaseType(fnType);
615 |     } else {
616 |       fnType = new FunctionBuilder(typeRegistry)
617 |           .withName(fnName)
618 |           .withSourceNode(contents.getSourceNode())
619 |           .withParamsNode(parametersNode)
620 |           .withReturnType(returnType, returnTypeInferred)
621 |           .withTypeOfThis(thisType)
622 |           .withTemplateNames(templateTypeNames)
623 |           .build();
624 |       maybeSetBaseType(fnType);
625 |     }
626 | 
627 |     if (implementedInterfaces != null) {
628 |       fnType.setImplementedInterfaces(implementedInterfaces);
629 |     }
630 | 
631 |     if (extendedInterfaces != null) {
632 |       fnType.setExtendedInterfaces(extendedInterfaces);
633 |     }
634 | 
635 |     typeRegistry.clearTemplateTypeNames();
636 | 
637 |     return fnType;
638 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocTokenStream.getJsDocToken()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocTokenStream.java
Original range: 58-194
Documentation:
/**
   * Tokenizes JSDoc comments.
   */
Method code:
58 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
59 |   final JsDocToken getJsDocToken() {
60 |     int c;
61 |     stringBufferTop = 0;
62 |     for (;;) {
63 |       // eat white spaces
64 |       for (;;) {
65 |         charno = -1;
66 |         c = getChar();
67 |         if (c == EOF_CHAR) {
68 |           return JsDocToken.EOF;
69 |         } else if (c == '\n') {
70 |           return JsDocToken.EOL;
71 |         } else if (!isJSSpace(c)) {
72 |           break;
73 |         }
74 |       }
75 | 
76 |       switch (c) {
77 |         // annotation, e.g. @type or @constructor
78 |         case '@':
79 |           do {
80 |             c = getChar();
81 |             if (isAlpha(c)) {
82 |               addToString(c);
83 |             } else {
84 |               ungetChar(c);
85 |               this.string = getStringFromBuffer();
86 |               stringBufferTop = 0;
87 |               return JsDocToken.ANNOTATION;
88 |             }
89 |           } while (true);
90 | 
91 |         case '*':
92 |           if (matchChar('/')) {
93 |             return JsDocToken.EOC;
94 |           } else {
95 |             return JsDocToken.STAR;
96 |           }
97 | 
98 |         case ',':
99 |           return JsDocToken.COMMA;
100 | 
101 |         case '>':
102 |           return JsDocToken.GT;
103 | 
104 |         case '(':
105 |           return JsDocToken.LP;
106 | 
107 |         case ')':
108 |           return JsDocToken.RP;
109 | 
110 |         case '{':
111 |           return JsDocToken.LC;
112 | 
113 |         case '}':
114 |           return JsDocToken.RC;
115 | 
116 |         case '[':
117 |           return JsDocToken.LB;
118 | 
119 |         case ']':
120 |           return JsDocToken.RB;
121 | 
122 |         case '?':
123 |           return JsDocToken.QMARK;
124 | 
125 |         case '!':
126 |           return JsDocToken.BANG;
127 | 
128 |         case ':':
129 |           return JsDocToken.COLON;
130 | 
131 |         case '=':
132 |           return JsDocToken.EQUALS;
133 | 
134 |         case '|':
135 |           matchChar('|');
136 |           return JsDocToken.PIPE;
137 | 
138 |         case '.':
139 |           c = getChar();
140 |           if (c == '<') {
141 |             return JsDocToken.LT;
142 |           } else {
143 |             if (c == '.') {
144 |               c = getChar();
145 |               if (c == '.') {
146 |                 return JsDocToken.ELLIPSIS;
147 |               } else {
148 |                 addToString('.');
149 |               }
150 |             }
151 |             // we may backtrack across line boundary
152 |             ungetBuffer[ungetCursor++] = c;
153 |             c = '.';
154 |           }
155 |           // fall through
156 | 
157 |         default: {
158 |           // recognize a JsDoc string but discard last . if it is followed by
159 |           // a non-JsDoc comment char, e.g. Array.<
160 |           int c1 = c;
161 |           addToString(c);
162 |           int c2 = getChar();
163 |           if (!isJSDocString(c2)) {
164 |             ungetChar(c2);
165 |             this.string = getStringFromBuffer();
166 |             stringBufferTop = 0;
167 |             return JsDocToken.STRING;
168 |           } else {
169 |             do {
170 |               c1 = c2;
171 |               c2 = getChar();
172 |               if (c1 == '.' && c2 == '<') {
173 |                 ungetChar(c2);
174 |                 ungetChar(c1);
175 |                 this.string = getStringFromBuffer();
176 |                 stringBufferTop = 0;
177 |                 return JsDocToken.STRING;
178 |               } else {
179 |                 if (isJSDocString(c2)) {
180 |                   addToString(c1);
181 |                 } else {
182 |                   ungetChar(c2);
183 |                   addToString(c1);
184 |                   this.string = getStringFromBuffer();
185 |                   stringBufferTop = 0;
186 |                   return JsDocToken.STRING;
187 |                 }
188 |               }
189 |             } while (true);
190 |           }
191 |         }
192 |       }
193 |     }
194 |   }

392 |     // properties.

394 |       passes.add(disambiguateProperties);
395 |     }

397 |     if (options.computeFunctionSideEffects) {
398 |       passes.add(markPureFunctions);
399 |     } else if (options.markNoSideEffectCalls) {
400 |       // TODO(user) The properties that this pass adds to CALL and NEW
401 |       // AST nodes increase the AST's in-memory size.  Given that we are
402 |       // already running close to our memory limits, we could run into
403 |       // trouble if we end up using the @nosideeffects annotation a lot
404 |       // or compute @nosideeffects annotations by looking at function
405 |       // bodies.  It should be easy to propagate @nosideeffects
406 |       // annotations as part of passes that depend on this property and
407 |       // store the result outside the AST (which would allow garbage

414 |     }

444 |     // it confuses crossModuleCodeMotion ability to recognized that

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.evaluatesToLocalValue(Node,Predicate<Node>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 2901-2965

/**
   * @param locals A predicate to apply to unknown local values.
   * @return Whether the node is known to be a value that is not a reference
   *     outside the expression scope.
   */
Method code:
2901 |   static boolean evaluatesToLocalValue(Node value, Predicate<Node> locals) {
2902 |     switch (value.getType()) {
2903 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
2904 |         // A result that is aliased by a non-local name, is the effectively the
2905 |         // same as returning a non-local name, but this doesn't matter if the
2906 |         // value is immutable.
2907 |         return NodeUtil.isImmutableValue(value.getLastChild())
2908 |             || (locals.apply(value)
2909 |                 && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals));
2910 |       case Token.COMMA:
2911 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2912 |       case Token.AND:
2913 |       case Token.OR:
2914 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild(), locals)
2915 |            && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2916 |       case Token.HOOK:
2917 |         return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild().getNext(), locals)
2918 |            && evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getLastChild(), locals);
2919 |       case Token.INC:
2920 |       case Token.DEC:
2921 |         if (value.getBooleanProp(Node.INCRDECR_PROP)) {
2922 |           return evaluatesToLocalValue(value.getFirstChild(), locals);
2923 |         } else {
2924 |           return true;
2925 |         }
2926 |       case Token.THIS:
2927 |         return locals.apply(value);
2928 |       case Token.NAME:
2929 |         return isImmutableValue(value) || locals.apply(value);
2930 |       case Token.GETELEM:
2931 |       case Token.GETPROP:
2932 |         // There is no information about the locality of object properties.
2933 |         return locals.apply(value);
2934 |       case Token.CALL:
2935 |         return callHasLocalResult(value)
2936 |             || isToStringMethodCall(value)
2937 |             || locals.apply(value);
2938 |       case Token.NEW:
2939 |         return newHasLocalResult(value)
2940 |                || locals.apply(value);
2941 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
2942 |       case Token.REGEXP:
2943 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
2944 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
2945 |         // Literals objects with non-literal children are allowed.
2946 |         return true;
2947 |       case Token.DELPROP:
2948 |       case Token.IN:
2949 |         // TODO(johnlenz): should IN operator be included in #isSimpleOperator?
2950 |         return true;
2951 |       default:
2952 |         // Other op force a local value:
2953 |         //  x = '' + g (x is now an local string)
2954 |         //  x -= g (x is now an local number)
2955 |         if (isAssignmentOp(value)
2956 |             || isSimpleOperator(value)
2957 |             || isImmutableValue(value)) {
2958 |           return true;
2959 |         }
2960 | 
2961 |         throw new IllegalStateException(
2962 |             "Unexpected expression node" + value +
2963 |             "\n parent:" + value.getParent());
2964 |     }
2965 |   }

   * @returns false iff the result of the expression is not consumed.

3110 |   static boolean isExpressionResultUsed(Node expr) {
3111 |     // TODO(johnlenz): consider sharing some code with trySimpleUnusedResult.
3112 |     Node parent = expr.getParent();
3113 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
3114 |       case Token.BLOCK:
3115 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
3116 |         return false;
3117 |       case Token.HOOK:
3118 |       case Token.AND:
3119 |       case Token.OR:

3128 |           // expression to a comma to be a no-op if it's used to indirect
3129 |           // an eval. This we pretend that this is "used".

3133 |               "eval".equals(expr.getNext().getString())) {

===== M0148 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.analyze(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 201-229
Documentation:
/**
   * Finds a fixed-point solution. The function has the side effect of replacing
   * the existing node annotations with the computed solutions using {@link
   * com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.GraphNode#setAnnotation(Annotation)}.
   *
   * <p>Initially, each node's input and output flow state contains the value
   * given by {@link #createInitialEstimateLattice()} (with the exception of the
   * entry node of the graph which takes on the {@link #createEntryLattice()}
   * value. Each node will use the output state of its predecessor and compute a
   * output state according to the instruction. At that time, any nodes that
   * depends on the node's newly modified output value will need to recompute
   * their output state again. Each step will perform a computation at one node
   * until no extra computation will modify any existing output state anymore.
   *
   * @param maxSteps Max number of iterations before the method stops and throw
   *        a {@link MaxIterationsExceededException}. This will prevent the
   *        analysis from going into a infinite loop.
   */
Method code:
201 |   final void analyze(int maxSteps) {
202 |     initialize();
203 |     int step = 0;
204 |     while (!orderedWorkSet.isEmpty()) {
205 |       if (step > maxSteps) {
206 |         throw new MaxIterationsExceededException(
207 |           "Analysis did not terminate after " + maxSteps + " iterations");
208 |       }
209 |       DiGraphNode<N, Branch> curNode = orderedWorkSet.iterator().next();
210 |       orderedWorkSet.remove(curNode);
211 |       joinInputs(curNode);
212 |       if (flow(curNode)) {
213 |         // If there is a change in the current node, we want to grab the list
214 |         // of nodes that this node affects.
215 |         List<DiGraphNode<N, Branch>> nextNodes = isForward() ?
216 |             cfg.getDirectedSuccNodes(curNode) :
217 |             cfg.getDirectedPredNodes(curNode);
218 |         for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> nextNode : nextNodes) {
219 |           if (nextNode != cfg.getImplicitReturn()) {
220 |             orderedWorkSet.add(nextNode);
221 |           }
222 |         }
223 |       }
224 |       step++;
225 |     }
226 |     if (isForward()) {
227 |       joinInputs(getCfg().getImplicitReturn());
228 |     }
229 |   }

/**
   * Expect that the given variable has not been declared with a type.
   *
   * @param sourceName The name of the source file we're in.
   * @param n The node where warnings should point to.
   * @param parent The parent of {@code n}.
   * @param var The variable that we're checking.
   * @param variableName The name of the variable.
   * @param newType The type being applied to the variable. Mostly just here
   *     for the benefit of the warning.
   * @return The variable we end up with. Most of the time, this will just
   *     be {@code var}, but in some rare cases we will need to declare
   *     a new var with new source info.
   */
Method code:
514 |   Var expectUndeclaredVariable(String sourceName, CompilerInput input,
515 |       Node n, Node parent, Var var, String variableName, JSType newType) {
516 |     Var newVar = var;
517 |     boolean allowDupe = false;
518 |     if (n.isGetProp() ||
519 |         NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(n, parent)) {
520 |       JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
521 |       if (info == null) {
522 |         info = parent.getJSDocInfo();
523 |       }
524 |       allowDupe =
525 |           info != null && info.getSuppressions().contains("duplicate");
526 |     }
527 | 
528 |     JSType varType = var.getType();
529 | 
530 |     // Only report duplicate declarations that have types. Other duplicates
531 |     // will be reported by the syntactic scope creator later in the
532 |     // compilation process.
533 |     if (varType != null &&
534 |         varType != typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE) &&
535 |         newType != null &&
536 |         newType != typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE)) {
537 |       // If there are two typed declarations of the same variable, that
538 |       // is an error and the second declaration is ignored, except in the
539 |       // case of native types. A null input type means that the declaration
540 |       // was made in TypedScopeCreator#createInitialScope and is a
541 |       // native type. We should redeclare it at the new input site.
542 |       if (var.input == null) {
543 |         Scope s = var.getScope();
544 |         s.undeclare(var);
545 |         newVar = s.declare(variableName, n, varType, input, false);
546 | 
547 |         n.setJSType(varType);
548 |         if (parent.isVar()) {
549 |           if (n.getFirstChild() != null) {
550 |             n.getFirstChild().setJSType(varType);
551 |           }
552 |         } else {
553 |           Preconditions.checkState(parent.isFunction());
554 |           parent.setJSType(varType);
555 |         }
556 |       } else {
557 |         // Always warn about duplicates if the overridden type does not
558 |         // match the original type.
559 |         //
560 |         // If the types match, suppress the warning iff there was a @suppress
561 |         // tag, or if the original declaration was a stub.
562 |         if (!(allowDupe ||
563 |               var.getParentNode().isExprResult()) ||
564 |             !newType.equals(varType)) {
565 |           report(JSError.make(sourceName, n, DUP_VAR_DECLARATION,
566 |               variableName, newType.toString(), var.getInputName(),
567 |               String.valueOf(var.nameNode.getLineno()),
568 |               varType.toString()));
569 |         }
570 |       }
571 |     }
572 | 
573 |     return newVar;
574 |   }

1262 |     // node in an expression (which therefore needs to have a type
1263 |     // assigned for it) versus some other decorative node that we
1264 |     // can safely ignore.  Function names, arguments (children of LP nodes) and
1265 |     // variable declarations are ignored.
1266 |     // TODO(user): remove this short-circuiting in favor of a
1267 |     // pre order traversal of the FUNCTION, CATCH, LP and VAR nodes.
1268 |     int parentNodeType = parent.getType();
1269 |     if (parentNodeType == Token.FUNCTION ||
1270 |         parentNodeType == Token.CATCH ||
1271 |         parentNodeType == Token.PARAM_LIST ||
1272 |         parentNodeType == Token.VAR) {
1273 |       return false;
1274 |     }
1275 | 
1276 |     JSType type = n.getJSType();
1277 |     if (type == null) {
1278 |       type = getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE);
1279 |       Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
1280 |       if (var != null) {
1281 |         JSType varType = var.getType();

1283 |           type = varType;
1284 |         }
1285 |       }
1286 |     }
1287 |     ensureTyped(t, n, type);
1288 |     return true;
1289 |   }

===== M0192 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType.isSubtype(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/JSType.java
Original range: 1051-1053
Documentation:
/**
   * Checks whether {@code this} is a subtype of {@code that}.<p>
   *
   * Subtyping rules:
   * <ul>
   * <li>(unknown) &mdash; every type is a subtype of the Unknown type.</li>
   * <li>(no) &mdash; the No type is a subtype of every type.</li>
   * <li>(no-object) &mdash; the NoObject type is a subtype of every object
   * type (i.e. subtypes of the Object type).</li>
   * <li>(ref) &mdash; a type is a subtype of itself.</li>
   * <li>(union-l) &mdash; A union type is a subtype of a type U if all the
   * union type's constituents are a subtype of U. Formally<br>
   * {@code (T<sub>1</sub>, &hellip;, T<sub>n</sub>) &lt;: U} if and only
   * {@code T<sub>k</sub> &lt;: U} for all {@code k &isin; 1..n}.</li>
   * <li>(union-r) &mdash; A type U is a subtype of a union type if it is a
   * subtype of one of the union type's constituents. Formally<br>
   * {@code U &lt;: (T<sub>1</sub>, &hellip;, T<sub>n</sub>)} if and only
   * if {@code U &lt;: T<sub>k</sub>} for some index {@code k}.</li>
   * <li>(objects) &mdash; an Object {@code O<sub>1</sub>} is a subtype
   * of an object {@code O<sub>2</sub>} if it has more properties
   * than {@code O<sub>2</sub>} and all common properties are
   * pairwise subtypes.</li>
   * </ul>
   *
   * @return {@code this &lt;: that}
   */
Method code:
1051 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {
1052 |     return isSubtypeHelper(this, that);
1053 |   }

/**
   * Merges the line number and character number in one integer. The Character
   * number takes the first 12 bits and the line number takes the rest. If
   * the character number is greater than <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code> it is
   * adjusted to <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code>.
   */
Method code:
1195 |   protected static int mergeLineCharNo(int lineno, int charno) {
1196 |     if (lineno < 0 || charno < 0) {

1199 |       return lineno << COLUMN_BITS | COLUMN_MASK;

1202 |     }

/**
   * TypeName := NameExpression | NameExpression TypeApplication
   * TypeApplication := '.<' TypeExpressionList '>'
   * TypeExpressionList := TypeExpression // a white lie
   */
Method code:
1766 |   private Node parseTypeName(JsDocToken token) {
1767 |     if (token != JsDocToken.STRING) {
1768 |       return reportGenericTypeSyntaxWarning();
1769 |     }
1770 | 
1771 |     String typeName = stream.getString();
1772 |     int lineno = stream.getLineno();
1773 |     int charno = stream.getCharno();
1774 |     while (match(JsDocToken.EOL) &&
1775 |         typeName.charAt(typeName.length() - 1) == '.') {
1776 |       skipEOLs();
1777 |       if (match(JsDocToken.STRING)) {
1778 |         next();
1779 |         typeName += stream.getString();
1780 |       }
1781 |     }
1782 | 
1783 |     Node typeNameNode = newStringNode(typeName, lineno, charno);
1784 | 
1785 |     if (match(JsDocToken.LT)) {
1786 |       next();
1787 |       skipEOLs();
1788 |       Node memberType = parseTypeExpressionList(next());
1789 |       if (memberType != null) {
1790 |         typeNameNode.addChildToFront(memberType);
1791 | 
1792 |         skipEOLs();
1793 |         if (!match(JsDocToken.GT)) {
1794 |           return reportTypeSyntaxWarning("msg.jsdoc.missing.gt");
1795 |         }
1796 | 
1797 |         next();
1798 |       }
1799 |     }
1800 |     return typeNameNode;
1801 |   }

/**
   * Add a parameter to the param list.
   * @param builder A builder.
   * @param paramType The parameter type.
   * @param warnedAboutArgList Whether we've already warned about arg ordering
   *     issues (like if optional args appeared before required ones).
   * @param isOptional Is this an optional parameter?
   * @param isVarArgs Is this a var args parameter?
   * @return Whether a warning was emitted.
   */
Method code:
541 |   private boolean addParameter(FunctionParamBuilder builder,
542 |       JSType paramType, boolean warnedAboutArgList,
543 |       boolean isOptional, boolean isVarArgs) {
544 |     boolean emittedWarning = false;
545 |     if (isOptional) {
546 |       // Remembering that an optional parameter has been encountered
547 |       // so that if a non optional param is encountered later, an
548 |       // error can be reported.
549 |       if (!builder.addOptionalParams(paramType) && !warnedAboutArgList) {
550 |         reportWarning(VAR_ARGS_MUST_BE_LAST);
551 |         emittedWarning = true;

553 |     } else if (isVarArgs) {
554 |       if (!builder.addVarArgs(paramType) && !warnedAboutArgList) {
555 |         reportWarning(VAR_ARGS_MUST_BE_LAST);
556 |         emittedWarning = true;
557 |       }
558 |     } else {
559 |       if (!builder.addRequiredParams(paramType) && !warnedAboutArgList) {
560 |         // An optional parameter was seen and this argument is not an optional
561 |         // or var arg so it is an error.
562 |         if (builder.hasVarArgs()) {
563 |           reportWarning(VAR_ARGS_MUST_BE_LAST);
564 |         } else {

566 |         }
567 |         emittedWarning = true;
568 |       }
569 |     }
570 |     return emittedWarning;

===== M0227 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.ensurePropertyDefined(Node,JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 510-555
Documentation:
/**
   * Defines a property if the property has not been defined yet.
   */
Method code:
510 |   private void ensurePropertyDefined(Node getprop, JSType rightType) {
511 |     String propName = getprop.getLastChild().getString();
512 |     JSType nodeType = getJSType(getprop.getFirstChild());
513 |     ObjectType objectType = ObjectType.cast(
514 |         nodeType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined());
515 |     if (objectType == null) {
516 |       registry.registerPropertyOnType(propName, nodeType);
517 |     } else {
518 |       if (ensurePropertyDeclaredHelper(getprop, objectType)) {
519 |         return;
520 |       }
521 | 
522 |       if (!objectType.isPropertyTypeDeclared(propName)) {
523 |         // We do not want a "stray" assign to define an inferred property
524 |         // for every object of this type in the program. So we use a heuristic
525 |         // approach to determine whether to infer the property.
526 |         //
527 |         // 1) If the property is already defined, join it with the previously
528 |         //    inferred type.
529 |         // 2) If this isn't an instance object, define it.
530 |         // 3) If the property of an object is being assigned in the constructor,
531 |         //    define it.
532 |         // 4) If this is a stub, define it.
533 |         // 5) Otherwise, do not define the type, but declare it in the registry
534 |         //    so that we can use it for missing property checks.
535 |         if (objectType.hasProperty(propName) ||
536 |             !objectType.isInstanceType()) {
537 |           if ("prototype".equals(propName)) {
538 |             objectType.defineDeclaredProperty(
539 |                 propName, rightType, getprop);
540 |           } else {
541 |             objectType.defineInferredProperty(
542 |                 propName, rightType, getprop);
543 |           }
544 |         } else {
545 |           if (getprop.getFirstChild().isThis() &&
546 |               getJSType(syntacticScope.getRootNode()).isConstructor()) {
547 |             objectType.defineInferredProperty(
548 |                 propName, rightType, getprop);
549 |           } else {
550 |             registry.registerPropertyOnType(propName, objectType);
551 |           }
552 |         }
553 |       }
554 |     }
555 |   }

/** Test if all characters in the string are in the Basic Latin (aka ASCII)
   * character set - that they have UTF-16 values equal to or below 0x7f.
   * This check can find which identifiers with Unicode characters need to be
   * escaped in order to allow resulting files to be processed by non-Unicode
   * aware UNIX tools and editors.
   * *
   * See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_characters_in_Unicode
   * for more on Basic Latin.
   *
   * @param s The string to be checked for ASCII-goodness.
   *
   * @return True if all characters in the string are in Basic Latin set.
   */
Method code:
2407 |   static boolean isLatin(String s) {
2408 |     char LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN = 0x7f;
2409 |     int len = s.length();
2410 |     for (int index = 0; index < len; index++) {
2411 |       char c = s.charAt(index);
2412 |       if (c > LARGEST_BASIC_LATIN) {
2413 |         return false;
2414 |       }
2415 |     }
2416 |     return true;
2417 |   }

===== M0260 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InferJSDocInfo.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InferJSDocInfo.java
Original range: 92-189
Documentation:

Method code:
92 |   @Override
93 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
94 |     JSDocInfo docInfo;
95 | 
96 |     switch (n.getType()) {
97 |       // Infer JSDocInfo on types of all type declarations on variables.
98 |       case Token.NAME:
99 |         if (parent == null) {
100 |           return;
101 |         }
102 | 
103 |         // Only allow JSDoc on VARs, function declarations, and assigns.
104 |         if (!parent.isVar() &&
105 |             !NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(parent) &&
106 |             !(parent.isAssign() &&
107 |               n == parent.getFirstChild())) {
108 |           return;
109 |         }
110 | 
111 |         // There are four places the doc info could live.
112 |         // 1) A FUNCTION node.
113 |         // /** ... */ function f() { ... }
114 |         // 2) An ASSIGN parent.
115 |         // /** ... */ x = function () { ... }
116 |         // 3) A NAME parent.
117 |         // var x, /** ... */ y = function() { ... }
118 |         // 4) A VAR gramps.
119 |         // /** ... */ var x = function() { ... }
120 |         docInfo = n.getJSDocInfo();
121 |         if (docInfo == null &&
122 |             !(parent.isVar() &&
123 |                 !parent.hasOneChild())) {
124 |           docInfo = parent.getJSDocInfo();
125 |         }
126 | 
127 |         // Try to find the type of the NAME.
128 |         JSType varType = n.getJSType();
129 |         if (varType == null && parent.isFunction()) {
130 |           varType = parent.getJSType();
131 |         }
132 | 
133 |         // If we have no type to attach JSDocInfo to, then there's nothing
134 |         // we can do.
135 |         if (varType == null || docInfo == null) {
136 |           return;
137 |         }
138 | 
139 |         // Dereference the type. If the result is not an object, or already
140 |         // has docs attached, then do nothing.
141 |         ObjectType objType = dereferenceToObject(varType);
142 |         if (objType == null || objType.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
143 |           return;
144 |         }
145 | 
146 |         attachJSDocInfoToNominalTypeOrShape(objType, docInfo, n.getString());
147 |         break;
148 | 
149 |       case Token.GETPROP:
150 |         // Infer JSDocInfo on properties.
151 |         // There are two ways to write doc comments on a property.
152 |         //
153 |         // 1)
154 |         // /** @deprecated */
155 |         // obj.prop = ...
156 |         //
157 |         // 2)
158 |         // /** @deprecated */
159 |         // obj.prop;
160 |         if (parent.isExprResult() ||
161 |             (parent.isAssign() &&
162 |              parent.getFirstChild() == n)) {
163 |           docInfo = n.getJSDocInfo();
164 |           if (docInfo == null) {
165 |             docInfo = parent.getJSDocInfo();
166 |           }
167 |           if (docInfo != null) {
168 |             ObjectType lhsType =
169 |                 dereferenceToObject(n.getFirstChild().getJSType());
170 |             if (lhsType != null) {
171 |               // Put the JSDoc in the property slot, if there is one.
172 |               String propName = n.getLastChild().getString();
173 |               if (lhsType.hasOwnProperty(propName)) {
174 |                 lhsType.setPropertyJSDocInfo(propName, docInfo);
175 |               }
176 | 
177 |               // Put the JSDoc in any constructors or function shapes as well.
178 |               ObjectType propType =
179 |                   dereferenceToObject(lhsType.getPropertyType(propName));
180 |               if (propType != null) {
181 |                 attachJSDocInfoToNominalTypeOrShape(
182 |                     propType, docInfo, n.getQualifiedName());
183 |               }
184 |             }
185 |           }
186 |         }
187 |         break;
188 |     }
189 |   }

/**
   * BasicTypeExpression := '*' | 'null' | 'undefined' | TypeName
   *     | FunctionType | UnionType | RecordType | ArrayType
   */
Method code:
1733 |   private Node parseBasicTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {
1734 |     if (token == JsDocToken.STAR) {
1735 |       return newNode(Token.STAR);
1736 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.LB) {
1737 |       skipEOLs();
1738 |       return parseArrayType(next());
1739 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.LC) {
1740 |       skipEOLs();
1741 |       return parseRecordType(next());
1742 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.LP) {
1743 |       skipEOLs();
1744 |       return parseUnionType(next());
1745 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.STRING) {
1746 |       String string = stream.getString();
1747 |       if ("function".equals(string)) {
1748 |         skipEOLs();
1749 |         return parseFunctionType(next());
1750 |       } else if ("null".equals(string) || "undefined".equals(string)) {
1751 |         return newStringNode(string);
1752 |       } else {
1753 |         return parseTypeName(token);
1754 |       }
1755 |     }
1756 | 
1757 |     restoreLookAhead(token);
1758 |     return reportGenericTypeSyntaxWarning();
1759 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CheckSideEffects.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CheckSideEffects.java
Original range: 83-131
Documentation:

Method code:
83 |   @Override
84 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
85 |     // VOID nodes appear when there are extra semicolons at the BLOCK level.
86 |     // I've been unable to think of any cases where this indicates a bug,
87 |     // and apparently some people like keeping these semicolons around,
88 |     // so we'll allow it.
89 |     if (n.isEmpty() ||
90 |         n.isComma()) {
91 |       return;
92 |     }
93 | 
94 |     if (parent == null) {
95 |       return;
96 |     }
97 | 
98 |     // Do not try to remove a block or an expr result. We already handle
99 |     // these cases when we visit the child, and the peephole passes will
100 |     // fix up the tree in more clever ways when these are removed.
101 |     if (n.isExprResult() || n.isBlock()) {
102 |       return;
103 |     }
104 | 
105 |     // This no-op statement was there so that JSDoc information could
106 |     // be attached to the name. This check should not complain about it.
107 |     if (n.isQualifiedName() && n.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
108 |       return;
109 |     }
110 | 
111 |     boolean isResultUsed = NodeUtil.isExpressionResultUsed(n);
112 |     boolean isSimpleOp = NodeUtil.isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType());
113 |     if (!isResultUsed &&
114 |         (isSimpleOp || !NodeUtil.mayHaveSideEffects(n, t.getCompiler()))) {
115 |       String msg = "This code lacks side-effects. Is there a bug?";
116 |       if (n.isString()) {
117 |         msg = "Is there a missing '+' on the previous line?";
118 |       } else if (isSimpleOp) {
119 |         msg = "The result of the '" + Token.name(n.getType()).toLowerCase() +
120 |             "' operator is not being used.";
121 |       }
122 | 
123 |       t.getCompiler().report(
124 |           t.makeError(n, level, USELESS_CODE_ERROR, msg));
125 |       // TODO(johnlenz): determine if it is necessary to
126 |       // try to protect side-effect free statements as well.
127 |       if (!NodeUtil.isStatement(n)) {
128 |         problemNodes.add(n);
129 |       }
130 |     }
131 |   }

===== M0342 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypedScopeCreator.AbstractScopeBuilder.isQualifiedNameInferred(String,Node,JSDocInfo,Node,JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypedScopeCreator.java
Original range: 1604-1647
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines whether a qualified name is inferred.
     * NOTE(nicksantos): Determining whether a property is declared or not
     * is really really obnoxious.
     *
     * The problem is that there are two (equally valid) coding styles:
     *
     * (function() {
     *   /* The authoritative definition of goog.bar. /
     *   goog.bar = function() {};
     * })();
     *
     * function f() {
     *   goog.bar();
     *   /* Reset goog.bar to a no-op. /
     *   goog.bar = function() {};
     * }
     *
     * In a dynamic language with first-class functions, it's very difficult
     * to know which one the user intended without looking at lots of
     * contextual information (the second example demonstrates a small case
     * of this, but there are some really pathological cases as well).
     *
     * The current algorithm checks if either the declaration has
     * JsDoc type information, or @const with a known type,
     * or a function literal with a name we haven't seen before.
     */
Method code:
1604 |     private boolean isQualifiedNameInferred(
1605 |         String qName, Node n, JSDocInfo info,
1606 |         Node rhsValue, JSType valueType) {
1607 |       if (valueType == null) {
1608 |         return true;
1609 |       }
1610 | 
1611 |       boolean inferred = true;
1612 |       if (info != null) {
1613 |         inferred = !(info.hasType()
1614 |             || info.hasEnumParameterType()
1615 |             || (info.isConstant() && valueType != null
1616 |                 && !valueType.isUnknownType())
1617 |             || FunctionTypeBuilder.isFunctionTypeDeclaration(info));
1618 |       }
1619 | 
1620 |       if (inferred && rhsValue != null && rhsValue.isFunction()) {
1621 |         if (info != null) {
1622 |           return false;
1623 |         } else if (!scope.isDeclared(qName, false) &&
1624 |             n.isUnscopedQualifiedName()) {
1625 | 
1626 |           // Check if this is in a conditional block.
1627 |           // Functions assigned in conditional blocks are inferred.
1628 |           for (Node current = n.getParent();
1629 |                !(current.isScript() || current.isFunction());
1630 |                current = current.getParent()) {
1631 |             if (NodeUtil.isControlStructure(current)) {
1632 |               return true;
1633 |             }
1634 |           }
1635 | 
1636 |           // Check if this is assigned in an inner scope.
1637 |           // Functions assigned in inner scopes are inferred.
1638 |           AstFunctionContents contents =
1639 |               getFunctionAnalysisResults(scope.getRootNode());
1640 |           if (contents == null ||
1641 |               !contents.getEscapedQualifiedNames().contains(qName)) {
1642 |             return false;
1643 |           }
1644 |         }
1645 |       }
1646 |       return inferred;
1647 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.UnionTypeBuilder.addAlternate(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/UnionTypeBuilder.java
Original range: 121-214
Documentation:
/**
   * Adds an alternate to the union type under construction. Returns this
   * for easy chaining.
   */
Method code:
121 |   UnionTypeBuilder addAlternate(JSType alternate) {
122 |     // build() returns the bottom type by default, so we can
123 |     // just bail out early here.
124 |     if (alternate.isNoType()) {
125 |       return this;
126 |     }
127 | 
128 |     isAllType = isAllType || alternate.isAllType();
129 | 
130 |     boolean isAlternateUnknown = alternate instanceof UnknownType;
131 |     isNativeUnknownType = isNativeUnknownType || isAlternateUnknown;
132 |     if (isAlternateUnknown) {
133 |       areAllUnknownsChecked = areAllUnknownsChecked &&
134 |           alternate.isCheckedUnknownType();
135 |     }
136 |     if (!isAllType && !isNativeUnknownType) {
137 |       if (alternate.isUnionType()) {
138 |         UnionType union = alternate.toMaybeUnionType();
139 |         for (JSType unionAlt : union.getAlternates()) {
140 |           addAlternate(unionAlt);
141 |         }
142 |       } else {
143 |         if (alternates.size() > maxUnionSize) {
144 |           return this;
145 |         }
146 | 
147 |         // Function types are special, because they have their
148 |         // own bizarre sub-lattice. See the comments on
149 |         // FunctionType#supAndInf helper and above at functionTypePosition.
150 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType() && functionTypePosition != -1) {
151 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
152 |           FunctionType other =
153 |               alternates.get(functionTypePosition).toMaybeFunctionType();
154 |           FunctionType supremum =
155 |               alternate.toMaybeFunctionType().supAndInfHelper(other, true);
156 |           alternates.set(functionTypePosition, supremum);
157 |           result = null;
158 |           return this;
159 |         }
160 | 
161 |         // Look through the alternates we've got so far,
162 |         // and check if any of them are duplicates of
163 |         // one another.
164 |         int currentIndex = 0;
165 |         Iterator<JSType> it = alternates.iterator();
166 |         while (it.hasNext()) {
167 |           JSType current = it.next();
168 | 
169 |           // Unknown and NoResolved types may just be names that haven't
170 |           // been resolved yet. So keep these in the union, and just use
171 |           // equality checking for simple de-duping.
172 |           if (alternate.isUnknownType() ||
173 |               current.isUnknownType() ||
174 |               alternate.isNoResolvedType() ||
175 |               current.isNoResolvedType() ||
176 |               alternate.hasAnyTemplate() ||
177 |               current.hasAnyTemplate()) {
178 |             if (alternate.isEquivalentTo(current)) {
179 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
180 |               return this;
181 |             }
182 |           } else {
183 |             if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
184 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
185 |               return this;
186 |             } else if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
187 |               // Alternate makes current obsolete
188 |               it.remove();
189 | 
190 |               if (currentIndex == functionTypePosition) {
191 |                 functionTypePosition = -1;
192 |               } else if (currentIndex < functionTypePosition) {
193 |                 functionTypePosition--;
194 |                 currentIndex--;
195 |               }
196 |             }
197 |           }
198 |           currentIndex++;
199 |         }
200 | 
201 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType()) {
202 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
203 |           Preconditions.checkState(functionTypePosition == -1);
204 |           functionTypePosition = alternates.size();
205 |         }
206 | 
207 |         alternates.add(alternate);
208 |         result = null; // invalidate the memoized result
209 |       }
210 |     } else {
211 |       result = null;
212 |     }
213 |     return this;
214 |   }

===== M0370 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.SyntacticScopeCreator.scanVars(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/SyntacticScopeCreator.java
Original range: 124-178
Documentation:
/**
   * Scans and gather variables declarations under a Node
   */
Method code:
124 |   private void scanVars(Node n, Node parent) {
125 |     switch (n.getType()) {
126 |       case Token.VAR:
127 |         // Declare all variables. e.g. var x = 1, y, z;
128 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
129 |              child != null;) {
130 |           Node next = child.getNext();
131 |           declareVar(child);
132 |           child = next;
133 |         }
134 |         return;
135 | 
136 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
137 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
138 |           return;
139 |         }
140 | 
141 |         String fnName = n.getFirstChild().getString();
142 |         if (fnName.isEmpty()) {
143 |           // This is invalid, but allow it so the checks can catch it.
144 |           return;
145 |         }
146 |         declareVar(n.getFirstChild());
147 |         return;   // should not examine function's children
148 | 
149 |       case Token.CATCH:
150 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
151 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getFirstChild().isName());
152 |         // the first child is the catch var and the third child
153 |         // is the code block
154 | 
155 |         final Node var = n.getFirstChild();
156 |         final Node block = var.getNext();
157 | 
158 |         declareVar(var);
159 |         scanVars(block, n);
160 |         return;  // only one child to scan
161 | 
162 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
163 |         inputId = n.getInputId();
164 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(inputId);
165 |         break;
166 |     }
167 | 
168 |     // Variables can only occur in statement-level nodes, so
169 |     // we only need to traverse children in a couple special cases.
170 |     if (NodeUtil.isControlStructure(n) || NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(n)) {
171 |       for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
172 |            child != null;) {
173 |         Node next = child.getNext();
174 |         scanVars(child, n);
175 |         child = next;
176 |       }
177 |     }
178 |   }

   * Gets the value of a node as a String, or null if it cannot be converted.
   * When it returns a non-null String, this method effectively emulates the
   * <code>String()</code> JavaScript cast function.

177 |   static String getStringValue(Node n) {

1076 |   static boolean isSubtypeHelper(JSType thisType, JSType thatType) {
1077 |     // unknown
1078 |     if (thatType.isUnknownType()) {
1079 |       return true;
1080 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.NamedType.lookupViaProperties(ErrorReporter,StaticScope<JSType>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/NamedType.java
Original range: 290-324
Documentation:
/**
   * Resolves a type by looking up its first component in the scope, and
   * subsequent components as properties. The scope must have been fully
   * parsed and a symbol table constructed.
   * @return The type of the symbol, or null if the type could not be found.
   */
Method code:
290 |   private JSType lookupViaProperties( ErrorReporter t,
291 |       StaticScope<JSType> enclosing) {
292 |     String[] componentNames = reference.split("\\.", -1);
293 |     if (componentNames[0].length() == 0) {
294 |       return null;
295 |     }
296 |     StaticSlot<JSType> slot = enclosing.getSlot(componentNames[0]);
297 |     if (slot == null) {
298 |       return null;
299 |     }
300 |     // If the first component has a type of 'Unknown', then any type
301 |     // names using it should be regarded as silently 'Unknown' rather than be
302 |     // noisy about it.
303 |     JSType slotType = slot.getType();
304 |     if (slotType == null || slotType.isAllType() || slotType.isNoType()) {
305 |       return null;
306 |     }
307 |     JSType value = getTypedefType(t, slot, componentNames[0]);
308 |     if (value == null) {
309 |       return null;
310 |     }
311 | 
312 |     // resolving component by component
313 |     for (int i = 1; i < componentNames.length; i++) {
314 |       ObjectType parentClass = ObjectType.cast(value);
315 |       if (parentClass == null) {
316 |         return null;
317 |       }
318 |       if (componentNames[i].length() == 0) {
319 |         return null;
320 |       }
321 |       value = parentClass.getPropertyType(componentNames[i]);
322 |     }
323 |     return value;
324 |   }

===== M0414 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowGraph.java
Original range: 151-197
Documentation:
/**
   * @return True if n should be represented by a new CFG node in the control
   * flow graph.
   */
Method code:
151 |   public static boolean isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node n) {
152 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
153 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
154 |       case Token.BLOCK:
155 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
156 |       case Token.TRY:
157 |         return true;
158 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
159 |         // A function node represents the start of a function where the name
160 |         // is bleed into the local scope and parameters has been assigned
161 |         // to the formal argument names. The node includes the name of the
162 |         // function and the LP list since we assume the whole set up process
163 |         // is atomic without change in control flow. The next change of
164 |         // control is going into the function's body represent by the second
165 |         // child.
166 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
167 |       case Token.WHILE:
168 |       case Token.DO:
169 |       case Token.IF:
170 |         // Theses control structure is represented by its node that holds the
171 |         // condition. Each of them is a branch node based on its condition.
172 |         return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
173 | 
174 |       case Token.FOR:
175 |         // The FOR(;;) node differs from other control structure in that
176 |         // it has a initialization and a increment statement. Those
177 |         // two statements have its corresponding CFG nodes to represent them.
178 |         // The FOR node represents the condition check for each iteration.
179 |         // That way the following:
180 |         // for(var x = 0; x < 10; x++) { } has a graph that is isomorphic to
181 |         // var x = 0; while(x<10) {  x++; }
182 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
183 |           // TODO(user): Investigate how we should handle the case where
184 |           // we have a very complex expression inside the FOR-IN header.
185 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
186 |         } else {
187 |           return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
188 |         }
189 |       case Token.SWITCH:
190 |       case Token.CASE:
191 |       case Token.CATCH:
192 |       case Token.WITH:
193 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild();
194 |       default:
195 |         return false;
196 |     }
197 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.BuildGlobalNamespace.getValueType(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/GlobalNamespace.java
Original range: 513-535
Documentation:
/**
     * Gets the type of a value or simple expression.
     *
     * @param n An r-value in an assignment or variable declaration (not null)
     * @return A {@link Name.Type}
     */
Method code:
513 |     Name.Type getValueType(Node n) {
514 |       switch (n.getType()) {
515 |         case Token.OBJECTLIT:
516 |           return Name.Type.OBJECTLIT;
517 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
518 |           return Name.Type.FUNCTION;
519 |         case Token.OR:
520 |           // Recurse on the second value. If the first value were an object
521 |           // literal or function, then the OR would be meaningless and the
522 |           // second value would be dead code. Assume that if the second value
523 |           // is an object literal or function, then the first value will also
524 |           // evaluate to one when it doesn't evaluate to false.
525 |           return getValueType(n.getLastChild());
526 |         case Token.HOOK:
527 |           // The same line of reasoning used for the OR case applies here.
528 |           Node second = n.getFirstChild().getNext();
529 |           Name.Type t = getValueType(second);
530 |           if (t != Name.Type.OTHER) return t;
531 |           Node third = second.getNext();
532 |           return getValueType(third);
533 |       }
534 |       return Name.Type.OTHER;
535 |     }

134 |         } else {
135 |           return P1_GT_P2;
136 |         }
137 |       }
138 | 
139 |       // check level
140 |       if (p1.level != p2.level) {
141 |         return p2.level.compareTo(p1.level);
142 |       }
143 | 
144 |       // sourceName comparison
145 |       String source1 = p1.error.sourceName;
146 |       String source2 = p2.error.sourceName;
147 |       if (source1 != null && source2 != null) {
148 |         int sourceCompare = source1.compareTo(source2);
149 |         if (sourceCompare != 0) {
150 |           return sourceCompare;
151 |         }
152 |       } else if (source1 == null && source2 != null) {
153 |         return P1_LT_P2;
154 |       } else if (source1 != null && source2 == null) {
155 |         return P1_GT_P2;
156 |       }
157 |       // lineno comparison
158 |       int lineno1 = p1.error.lineNumber;
159 |       int lineno2 = p2.error.lineNumber;
160 |       if (lineno1 != lineno2) {
161 |         return lineno1 - lineno2;
162 |       } else if (lineno1 < 0 && 0 <= lineno2) {
163 |         return P1_LT_P2;
164 |       } else if (0 <= lineno1 && lineno2 < 0) {
165 |         return P1_GT_P2;
166 |       }
167 |       // charno comparison
168 |       int charno1 = p1.error.getCharno();
169 |       int charno2 = p2.error.getCharno();
170 |       if (charno1 != charno2) {
171 |         return charno1 - charno2;
172 |       } else if (charno1 < 0 && 0 <= charno2) {
173 |         return P1_LT_P2;
174 |       } else if (0 <= charno1 && charno2 < 0) {
175 |         return P1_GT_P2;
176 |       }
177 |       // description
178 |       return p1.error.description.compareTo(p2.error.description);
179 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.process(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 148-190
Documentation:

Method code:
148 |   @Override
149 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
150 |     this.root = root;
151 |     astPositionCounter = 0;
152 |     astPosition = Maps.newHashMap();
153 |     nodePriorities = Maps.newHashMap();
154 |     cfg = new AstControlFlowGraph(computeFallThrough(root), nodePriorities,
155 |                                   edgeAnnotations);
156 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, this);
157 |     astPosition.put(null, ++astPositionCounter); // the implicit return is last.
158 | 
159 |     // Now, generate the priority of nodes by doing a depth-first
160 |     // search on the CFG.
161 |     priorityCounter = 0;
162 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> entry = cfg.getEntry();
163 |     prioritizeFromEntryNode(entry);
164 | 
165 |     if (shouldTraverseFunctions) {
166 |       // If we're traversing inner functions, we need to rank the
167 |       // priority of them too.
168 |       for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
169 |         Node value = candidate.getValue();
170 |         if (value != null && value.isFunction()) {
171 |           Preconditions.checkState(
172 |               !nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate) || candidate == entry);
173 |           prioritizeFromEntryNode(candidate);
174 |         }
175 |       }
176 |     }
177 | 
178 |     // At this point, all reachable nodes have been given a priority, but
179 |     // unreachable nodes have not been given a priority. Put them last.
180 |     // Presumably, it doesn't really matter what priority they get, since
181 |     // this shouldn't happen in real code.
182 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
183 |       if (!nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate)) {
184 |         nodePriorities.put(candidate, ++priorityCounter);
185 |       }
186 |     }
187 | 
188 |     // Again, the implicit return node is always last.
189 |     nodePriorities.put(cfg.getImplicitReturn(), ++priorityCounter);
190 |   }

   *     '{' OptionalParameterType '}' |

   * Infer the parameter types from the list of argument names and
   * the doc info.
   */
Method code:
421 |   FunctionTypeBuilder inferParameterTypes(@Nullable Node argsParent,
422 |       @Nullable JSDocInfo info) {
423 |     if (argsParent == null) {
424 |       if (info == null) {
425 |         return this;
426 |       } else {
427 |         return inferParameterTypes(info);
428 |       }
429 |     }
430 | 
431 |     // arguments
432 |     Node oldParameterType = null;
433 |     if (parametersNode != null) {
434 |       oldParameterType = parametersNode.getFirstChild();
435 |     }
436 | 
437 |     FunctionParamBuilder builder = new FunctionParamBuilder(typeRegistry);
438 |     boolean warnedAboutArgList = false;
439 |     Set<String> allJsDocParams = (info == null) ?
440 |         Sets.<String>newHashSet() :
441 |         Sets.newHashSet(info.getParameterNames());
442 |     boolean foundTemplateType = false;
443 |     boolean isVarArgs = false;
444 |     for (Node arg : argsParent.children()) {
445 |       String argumentName = arg.getString();
446 |       allJsDocParams.remove(argumentName);
447 | 
448 |       // type from JSDocInfo
449 |       JSType parameterType = null;
450 |       boolean isOptionalParam = isOptionalParameter(arg, info);
451 |       isVarArgs = isVarArgsParameter(arg, info);

454 |         parameterType =
455 |             info.getParameterType(argumentName).evaluate(scope, typeRegistry);
456 |       } else if (oldParameterType != null &&
457 |           oldParameterType.getJSType() != null) {
458 |         parameterType = oldParameterType.getJSType();
459 |         isOptionalParam = oldParameterType.isOptionalArg();
460 |         isVarArgs = oldParameterType.isVarArgs();
461 |       } else {
462 |         parameterType = typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE);
463 |       }
464 | 
465 |       warnedAboutArgList |= addParameter(
466 |           builder, parameterType, warnedAboutArgList,
467 |           isOptionalParam,
468 |           isVarArgs);
469 | 
470 |       if (oldParameterType != null) {
471 |         oldParameterType = oldParameterType.getNext();
472 |       }
473 |     }
474 | 
475 |     // Copy over any old parameters that aren't in the param list.
476 |     if (!isVarArgs) {
477 |       while (oldParameterType != null && !isVarArgs) {
478 |         builder.newParameterFromNode(oldParameterType);
479 |         oldParameterType = oldParameterType.getNext();
480 |       }
481 |     }
482 | 
483 |     for (String inexistentName : allJsDocParams) {
484 |       reportWarning(INEXISTANT_PARAM, inexistentName, fnName);
485 |     }
486 | 
487 |     parametersNode = builder.build();

489 |   }

Method code:
389 |     @Override
390 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
391 |       if (isCallToScopeMethod(n)) {
392 |         validateScopeCall(t, n, n.getParent());
393 |       }
394 | 
395 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() < 2) {
396 |         return;
397 |       }
398 | 
399 |       int type = n.getType();
400 |       Var aliasVar = null;
401 |       if (type == Token.NAME) {
402 |         String name = n.getString();
403 |         Var lexicalVar = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
404 |         if (lexicalVar != null && lexicalVar == aliases.get(name)) {
405 |           aliasVar = lexicalVar;
406 |         }
407 |       }
408 | 
409 |       // Validate the top-level of the goog.scope block.
410 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() == 2) {
411 |         if (aliasVar != null && NodeUtil.isLValue(n)) {
412 |           if (aliasVar.getNode() == n) {
413 |             aliasDefinitionsInOrder.add(n);
414 | 
415 |             // Return early, to ensure that we don't record a definition
416 |             // twice.
417 |             return;
418 |           } else {
419 |             report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_ALIAS_REDEFINED, n.getString());
420 |           }
421 |         }
422 | 
423 |         if (type == Token.RETURN) {
424 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_USES_RETURN);
425 |         } else if (type == Token.THIS) {
426 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_REFERENCES_THIS);
427 |         } else if (type == Token.THROW) {
428 |           report(t, n, GOOG_SCOPE_USES_THROW);
429 |         }
430 |       }
431 | 
432 |       // Validate all descendent scopes of the goog.scope block.
433 |       if (t.getScopeDepth() >= 2) {
434 |         // Check if this name points to an alias.
435 |         if (aliasVar != null) {
436 |           // Note, to support the transitive case, it's important we don't
437 |           // clone aliasedNode here.  For example,
438 |           // var g = goog; var d = g.dom; d.createElement('DIV');
439 |           // The node in aliasedNode (which is "g") will be replaced in the
440 |           // changes pass above with "goog".  If we cloned here, we'd end up
441 |           // with <code>g.dom.createElement('DIV')</code>.
442 |           Node aliasedNode = aliasVar.getInitialValue();
443 |           aliasUsages.add(new AliasedNode(n, aliasedNode));
444 |         }
445 | 
446 |         JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
447 |         if (info != null) {
448 |           for (Node node : info.getTypeNodes()) {
449 |             fixTypeNode(node);
450 |           }
451 |         }
452 | 
453 |         // TODO(robbyw): Error for goog.scope not at root.
454 |       }
455 |     }
