Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.ArrowType.hasEqualParameters(ArrowType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/ArrowType.java
Original range: 177-200
Documentation:
/**
   * @return True if our parameter spec is equal to {@code that}'s parameter
   *     spec.
   */
Method code:
177 |   boolean hasEqualParameters(ArrowType that) {
178 |     Node thisParam = parameters.getFirstChild();
179 |     Node otherParam = that.parameters.getFirstChild();
180 |     while (thisParam != null && otherParam != null) {
181 |       JSType thisParamType = thisParam.getJSType();
182 |       JSType otherParamType = otherParam.getJSType();
183 |       if (thisParamType != null) {
184 |         // Both parameter lists give a type for this param, it should be equal
185 |         if (otherParamType != null &&
186 |             !thisParamType.isEquivalentTo(otherParamType)) {
187 |           return false;
188 |         }
189 |       } else {
190 |         if (otherParamType != null) {
191 |           return false;
192 |         }
193 |       }
194 |       thisParam = thisParam.getNext();
195 |       otherParam = otherParam.getNext();
196 |     }
197 |     // One of the parameters is null, so the types are only equal if both
198 |     // parameter lists are null (they are equal).
199 |     return thisParam == otherParam;
200 |   }

/**
   * Stop the trace.
   * This may only be done once and must be done from the same thread
   * that started it.
   * @param silence_threshold Traces for time less than silence_threshold
   * ms will be left out of the trace report. A value of -1 indicates
   * that the current ThreadTrace silence_threshold should be used.
   * @return The time that this trace actually ran
   */
Method code:
407 |   long stop(int silence_threshold) {
408 |     Preconditions.checkState(Thread.currentThread() == startThread);
409 | 
410 |     ThreadTrace trace = getThreadTrace();
411 |     // Do nothing if the thread trace was not initialized.
412 |     if (!trace.isInitialized()) {
413 |       return 0;
414 |     }
415 | 
416 |     stopTimeMs = clock.currentTimeMillis();
417 |     if (extraTracingValues != null) {
418 |       // We use extraTracingValues.length rather than
419 |       // extraTracingStatistics.size() because a new statistic may
420 |       // have been added
421 |       for (int i = 0; i < extraTracingValues.length; i++) {
422 |         long value = extraTracingStatistics.get(i).stop(startThread);
423 |         extraTracingValues[i] = value - extraTracingValues[i];
424 |       }
425 |     }
426 | 
427 |     // Do nothing if the thread trace was not initialized.
428 |     if (!trace.isInitialized()) {
429 |       return 0;
430 |     }
431 | 
432 |     trace.endEvent(this, silence_threshold);
433 |     return stopTimeMs - startTimeMs;
434 |   }

===== M0567 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeCheck.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeCheck.java
Original range: 461-810
Documentation:
/**
   * This is the meat of the type checking.  It is basically one big switch,
   * with each case representing one type of parse tree node.  The individual
   * cases are usually pretty straightforward.
   *
   * @param t The node traversal object that supplies context, such as the
   * scope chain to use in name lookups as well as error reporting.
   * @param n The node being visited.
   * @param parent The parent of the node n.
   */
Method code:
461 |   @Override
462 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
463 |     JSType childType;
464 |     JSType leftType, rightType;
465 |     Node left, right;
466 |     // To be explicitly set to false if the node is not typeable.
467 |     boolean typeable = true;
468 | 
469 |     switch (n.getType()) {
470 |       case Token.NAME:
471 |         typeable = visitName(t, n, parent);
472 |         break;
473 | 
474 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
475 |         // If this is under a FUNCTION node, it is a parameter list and can be
476 |         // ignored here.
477 |         if (!parent.isFunction()) {
478 |           ensureTyped(t, n, getJSType(n.getFirstChild()));
479 |         } else {
480 |           typeable = false;
481 |         }
482 |         break;
483 | 
484 |       case Token.COMMA:
485 |         ensureTyped(t, n, getJSType(n.getLastChild()));
486 |         break;
487 | 
488 |       case Token.TRUE:
489 |       case Token.FALSE:
490 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
491 |         break;
492 | 
493 |       case Token.THIS:
494 |         ensureTyped(t, n, t.getScope().getTypeOfThis());
495 |         break;
496 | 
497 |       case Token.NULL:
498 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NULL_TYPE);
499 |         break;
500 | 
501 |       case Token.NUMBER:
502 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NUMBER_TYPE);
503 |         break;
504 | 
505 |       case Token.STRING:
506 |         ensureTyped(t, n, STRING_TYPE);
507 |         break;
508 | 
509 |       case Token.STRING_KEY:
510 |         typeable = false;
511 |         break;
512 | 
513 |       case Token.GETTER_DEF:
514 |       case Token.SETTER_DEF:
515 |         // Object literal keys are handled with OBJECTLIT
516 |         break;
517 | 
518 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
519 |         ensureTyped(t, n, ARRAY_TYPE);
520 |         break;
521 | 
522 |       case Token.REGEXP:
523 |         ensureTyped(t, n, REGEXP_TYPE);
524 |         break;
525 | 
526 |       case Token.GETPROP:
527 |         visitGetProp(t, n, parent);
528 |         typeable = !(parent.isAssign() &&
529 |                      parent.getFirstChild() == n);
530 |         break;
531 | 
532 |       case Token.GETELEM:
533 |         visitGetElem(t, n);
534 |         // The type of GETELEM is always unknown, so no point counting that.
535 |         // If that unknown leaks elsewhere (say by an assignment to another
536 |         // variable), then it will be counted.
537 |         typeable = false;
538 |         break;
539 | 
540 |       case Token.VAR:
541 |         visitVar(t, n);
542 |         typeable = false;
543 |         break;
544 | 
545 |       case Token.NEW:
546 |         visitNew(t, n);
547 |         typeable = true;
548 |         break;
549 | 
550 |       case Token.CALL:
551 |         visitCall(t, n);
552 |         typeable = !parent.isExprResult();
553 |         break;
554 | 
555 |       case Token.RETURN:
556 |         visitReturn(t, n);
557 |         typeable = false;
558 |         break;
559 | 
560 |       case Token.DEC:
561 |       case Token.INC:
562 |         left = n.getFirstChild();
563 |         validator.expectNumber(
564 |             t, left, getJSType(left), "increment/decrement");
565 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NUMBER_TYPE);
566 |         break;
567 | 
568 |       case Token.NOT:
569 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
570 |         break;
571 | 
572 |       case Token.VOID:
573 |         ensureTyped(t, n, VOID_TYPE);
574 |         break;
575 | 
576 |       case Token.TYPEOF:
577 |         ensureTyped(t, n, STRING_TYPE);
578 |         break;
579 | 
580 |       case Token.BITNOT:
581 |         childType = getJSType(n.getFirstChild());
582 |         if (!childType.matchesInt32Context()) {
583 |           report(t, n, BIT_OPERATION, NodeUtil.opToStr(n.getType()),
584 |               childType.toString());
585 |         }
586 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NUMBER_TYPE);
587 |         break;
588 | 
589 |       case Token.POS:
590 |       case Token.NEG:
591 |         left = n.getFirstChild();
592 |         validator.expectNumber(t, left, getJSType(left), "sign operator");
593 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NUMBER_TYPE);
594 |         break;
595 | 
596 |       case Token.EQ:
597 |       case Token.NE:
598 |       case Token.SHEQ:
599 |       case Token.SHNE: {
600 |         leftType = getJSType(n.getFirstChild());
601 |         rightType = getJSType(n.getLastChild());
602 | 
603 |         // We do not want to warn about explicit comparisons to VOID. People
604 |         // often do this if they think their type annotations screwed up.
605 |         //
606 |         // We do want to warn about cases where people compare things like
607 |         // (Array|null) == (Function|null)
608 |         // because it probably means they screwed up.
609 |         //
610 |         // This heuristic here is not perfect, but should catch cases we
611 |         // care about without too many false negatives.
612 |         JSType leftTypeRestricted = leftType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
613 |         JSType rightTypeRestricted = rightType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
614 | 
615 |         TernaryValue result = TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
616 |         if (n.getType() == Token.EQ || n.getType() == Token.NE) {
617 |           result = leftTypeRestricted.testForEquality(
618 |               rightTypeRestricted);
619 |           if (n.isNE()) {
620 |             result = result.not();
621 |           }
622 |         } else {
623 |           // SHEQ or SHNE
624 |           if (!leftTypeRestricted.canTestForShallowEqualityWith(
625 |                   rightTypeRestricted)) {
626 |             result = n.getType() == Token.SHEQ ?
627 |                 TernaryValue.FALSE : TernaryValue.TRUE;
628 |           }
629 |         }
630 | 
631 |         if (result != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
632 |           report(t, n, DETERMINISTIC_TEST, leftType.toString(),
633 |               rightType.toString(), result.toString());
634 |         }
635 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
636 |         break;
637 |       }
638 | 
639 |       case Token.LT:
640 |       case Token.LE:
641 |       case Token.GT:
642 |       case Token.GE:
643 |         leftType = getJSType(n.getFirstChild());
644 |         rightType = getJSType(n.getLastChild());
645 |         if (rightType.isNumber()) {
646 |           validator.expectNumber(
647 |               t, n, leftType, "left side of numeric comparison");
648 |         } else if (leftType.isNumber()) {
649 |           validator.expectNumber(
650 |               t, n, rightType, "right side of numeric comparison");
651 |         } else if (leftType.matchesNumberContext() &&
652 |                    rightType.matchesNumberContext()) {
653 |           // OK.
654 |         } else {
655 |           // Whether the comparison is numeric will be determined at runtime
656 |           // each time the expression is evaluated. Regardless, both operands
657 |           // should match a string context.
658 |           String message = "left side of comparison";
659 |           validator.expectString(t, n, leftType, message);
660 |           validator.expectNotNullOrUndefined(
661 |               t, n, leftType, message, getNativeType(STRING_TYPE));
662 |           message = "right side of comparison";
663 |           validator.expectString(t, n, rightType, message);
664 |           validator.expectNotNullOrUndefined(
665 |               t, n, rightType, message, getNativeType(STRING_TYPE));
666 |         }
667 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
668 |         break;
669 | 
670 |       case Token.IN:
671 |         left = n.getFirstChild();
672 |         right = n.getLastChild();
673 |         leftType = getJSType(left);
674 |         rightType = getJSType(right);
675 |         validator.expectObject(t, n, rightType, "'in' requires an object");
676 |         validator.expectString(t, left, leftType, "left side of 'in'");
677 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
678 |         break;
679 | 
680 |       case Token.INSTANCEOF:
681 |         left = n.getFirstChild();
682 |         right = n.getLastChild();
683 |         leftType = getJSType(left);
684 |         rightType = getJSType(right).restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
685 | 
686 |         validator.expectAnyObject(
687 |             t, left, leftType, "deterministic instanceof yields false");
688 |         validator.expectActualObject(
689 |             t, right, rightType, "instanceof requires an object");
690 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
691 |         break;
692 | 
693 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
694 |         visitAssign(t, n);
695 |         typeable = false;
696 |         break;
697 | 
698 |       case Token.ASSIGN_LSH:
699 |       case Token.ASSIGN_RSH:
700 |       case Token.ASSIGN_URSH:
701 |       case Token.ASSIGN_DIV:
702 |       case Token.ASSIGN_MOD:
703 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITOR:
704 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITXOR:
705 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITAND:
706 |       case Token.ASSIGN_SUB:
707 |       case Token.ASSIGN_ADD:
708 |       case Token.ASSIGN_MUL:
709 |       case Token.LSH:
710 |       case Token.RSH:
711 |       case Token.URSH:
712 |       case Token.DIV:
713 |       case Token.MOD:
714 |       case Token.BITOR:
715 |       case Token.BITXOR:
716 |       case Token.BITAND:
717 |       case Token.SUB:
718 |       case Token.ADD:
719 |       case Token.MUL:
720 |         visitBinaryOperator(n.getType(), t, n);
721 |         break;
722 | 
723 |       case Token.DELPROP:
724 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
725 |         break;
726 | 
727 |       case Token.CASE:
728 |         JSType switchType = getJSType(parent.getFirstChild());
729 |         JSType caseType = getJSType(n.getFirstChild());
730 |         validator.expectSwitchMatchesCase(t, n, switchType, caseType);
731 |         typeable = false;
732 |         break;
733 | 
734 |       case Token.WITH: {
735 |         Node child = n.getFirstChild();
736 |         childType = getJSType(child);
737 |         validator.expectObject(
738 |             t, child, childType, "with requires an object");
739 |         typeable = false;
740 |         break;
741 |       }
742 | 
743 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
744 |         visitFunction(t, n);
745 |         break;
746 | 
747 |       // These nodes have no interesting type behavior.
748 |       case Token.LABEL:
749 |       case Token.LABEL_NAME:
750 |       case Token.SWITCH:
751 |       case Token.BREAK:
752 |       case Token.CATCH:
753 |       case Token.TRY:
754 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
755 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
756 |       case Token.BLOCK:
757 |       case Token.EMPTY:
758 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
759 |       case Token.CONTINUE:
760 |       case Token.DEBUGGER:
761 |       case Token.THROW:
762 |         typeable = false;
763 |         break;
764 | 
765 |       // These nodes require data flow analysis.
766 |       case Token.DO:
767 |       case Token.FOR:
768 |       case Token.IF:
769 |       case Token.WHILE:
770 |         typeable = false;
771 |         break;
772 | 
773 |       // These nodes are typed during the type inference.
774 |       case Token.AND:
775 |       case Token.HOOK:
776 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
777 |       case Token.OR:
778 |         if (n.getJSType() != null) { // If we didn't run type inference.
779 |           ensureTyped(t, n);
780 |         } else {
781 |           // If this is an enum, then give that type to the objectlit as well.
782 |           if ((n.isObjectLit())
783 |               && (parent.getJSType() instanceof EnumType)) {
784 |             ensureTyped(t, n, parent.getJSType());
785 |           } else {
786 |             ensureTyped(t, n);
787 |           }
788 |         }
789 |         if (n.isObjectLit()) {
790 |           for (Node key : n.children()) {
791 |             visitObjLitKey(t, key, n);
792 |           }
793 |         }
794 |         break;
795 | 
796 |       default:
797 |         report(t, n, UNEXPECTED_TOKEN, Token.name(n.getType()));
798 |         ensureTyped(t, n);
799 |         break;
800 |     }
801 | 
802 |     // Don't count externs since the user's code may not even use that part.
803 |     typeable = typeable && !inExterns;
804 | 
805 |     if (typeable) {
806 |       doPercentTypedAccounting(t, n);
807 |     }
808 | 
809 |     checkNoTypeCheckSection(n, false);
810 |   }

===== M0601 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.getFunctionName(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 430-449
Documentation:
/**
   * Gets the function's name. This method recognizes five forms:
   * <ul>
   * <li>{@code function name() ...}</li>
   * <li>{@code var name = function() ...}</li>
   * <li>{@code qualified.name = function() ...}</li>
   * <li>{@code var name2 = function name1() ...}</li>
   * <li>{@code qualified.name2 = function name1() ...}</li>
   * </ul>
   * In two last cases with named function expressions, the second name is
   * returned (the variable of qualified name).
   *
   * @param n a node whose type is {@link Token#FUNCTION}
   * @return the function's name, or {@code null} if it has no name
   */
Method code:
430 |   static String getFunctionName(Node n) {
431 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.isFunction());
432 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
433 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
434 |       case Token.NAME:
435 |         // var name = function() ...
436 |         // var name2 = function name1() ...
437 |         return parent.getQualifiedName();
438 | 
439 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
440 |         // qualified.name = function() ...
441 |         // qualified.name2 = function name1() ...
442 |         return parent.getFirstChild().getQualifiedName();
443 | 
444 |       default:
445 |         // function name() ...
446 |         String name = n.getFirstChild().getQualifiedName();
447 |         return name;
448 |     }
449 |   }

===== M0605 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeValidator.expectNotNullOrUndefined(NodeTraversal,Node,JSType,String,JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeValidator.java
Original range: 241-267
Documentation:
/**
   * Expect the type to be anything but the null or void type. If the
   * expectation is not met, issue a warning at the provided node's
   * source code position. Note that a union type that includes the
   * void type and at least one other type meets the expectation.
   * @return Whether the expectation was met.
   */
Method code:
241 |   boolean expectNotNullOrUndefined(
242 |       NodeTraversal t, Node n, JSType type, String msg, JSType expectedType) {
243 |     if (!type.isNoType() && !type.isUnknownType() &&
244 |         type.isSubtype(nullOrUndefined) &&
245 |         !containsForwardDeclaredUnresolvedName(type)) {
246 | 
247 |       // There's one edge case right now that we don't handle well, and
248 |       // that we don't want to warn about.
249 |       // if (this.x == null) {
250 |       //   this.initializeX();
251 |       //   this.x.foo();
252 |       // }
253 |       // In this case, we incorrectly type x because of how we
254 |       // infer properties locally. See issue 109.
255 |       // http://code.google.com/p/closure-compiler/issues/detail?id=109
256 |       //
257 |       // We do not do this inference globally.
258 |       if (n.isGetProp() &&
259 |           !t.inGlobalScope() && type.isNullType()) {
260 |         return true;
261 |       }
262 | 
263 |       mismatch(t, n, msg, type, expectedType);
264 |       return false;
265 |     }
266 |     return true;
267 |   }

===== M0643 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(Node,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 591-628
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if this is a literal value. We define a literal value
   * as any node that evaluates to the same thing regardless of when or
   * where it is evaluated. So /xyz/ and [3, 5] are literals, but
   * the name a is not.
   *
   * Function literals do not meet this definition, because they
   * lexically capture variables. For example, if you have
   * <code>
   * function() { return a; }
   * </code>
   * If it is evaluated in a different scope, then it
   * captures a different variable. Even if the function did not read
   * any captured variables directly, it would still fail this definition,
   * because it affects the lifecycle of variables in the enclosing scope.
   *
   * However, a function literal with respect to a particular scope is
   * a literal.
   *
   * @param includeFunctions If true, all function expressions will be
   *     treated as literals.
   */
Method code:
591 |   static boolean isLiteralValue(Node n, boolean includeFunctions) {
592 |     switch (n.getType()) {
593 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
594 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
595 |              child = child.getNext()) {
596 |           if ((!child.isEmpty()) && !isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
597 |             return false;
598 |           }
599 |         }
600 |         return true;
601 | 
602 |       case Token.REGEXP:
603 |         // Return true only if all children are const.
604 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
605 |              child = child.getNext()) {
606 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child, includeFunctions)) {
607 |             return false;
608 |           }
609 |         }
610 |         return true;
611 | 
612 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
613 |         // Return true only if all values are const.
614 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
615 |              child = child.getNext()) {
616 |           if (!isLiteralValue(child.getFirstChild(), includeFunctions)) {
617 |             return false;
618 |           }
619 |         }
620 |         return true;
621 | 
622 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
623 |         return includeFunctions && !NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n);
624 | 
625 |       default:
626 |         return isImmutableValue(n);
627 |     }
628 |   }

613 |         // function f() { var x = 3; function g() { x = null } (x); }
614 |         boolean isInferred = var.isTypeInferred();
615 |         boolean unflowable = isInferred &&
616 |             isUnflowable(syntacticScope.getVar(varName));
617 | 
618 |         // 2) We're reading type information from another scope for an
619 |         // inferred variable.
620 |         // var t = null; function f() { (t); }
621 |         boolean nonLocalInferredSlot =
622 |             isInferred &&
623 |             syntacticScope.getParent() != null &&
624 |             var == syntacticScope.getParent().getSlot(varName);
625 | 
626 |         if (!unflowable && !nonLocalInferredSlot) {
627 |           type = var.getType();
628 |           if (type == null) {
629 |             type = getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE);
630 |           }
631 |         }
632 |       }
633 |     }
634 |     n.setJSType(type);
635 |     return scope;
636 |   }

===== M0685 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.handleStmtList(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 484-523
Documentation:

Method code:
484 |   private void handleStmtList(Node node) {
485 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
486 |     // Special case, don't add a block of empty CATCH block to the graph.
487 |     if (node.isBlock() && parent != null &&
488 |         parent.isTry() &&
489 |         NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node &&
490 |         !NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(node)) {
491 |       return;
492 |     }
493 | 
494 |     // A block transfer control to its first child if it is not empty.
495 |     Node child = node.getFirstChild();
496 | 
497 |     // Function declarations are skipped since control doesn't go into that
498 |     // function (unless it is called)
499 |     while (child != null && child.isFunction()) {
500 |       child = child.getNext();
501 |     }
502 | 
503 |     if (child != null) {
504 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFallThrough(child));
505 |     } else {
506 |       createEdge(node, Branch.UNCOND, computeFollowNode(node, this));
507 |     }
508 | 
509 |     // Synthetic blocks
510 |     if (parent != null) {
511 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
512 |         case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
513 |         case Token.CASE:
514 |         case Token.TRY:
515 |           break;
516 |         default:
517 |           if (node.isBlock() && node.isSyntheticBlock()) {
518 |             createEdge(node, Branch.SYN_BLOCK, computeFollowNode(node, this));
519 |           }
520 |           break;
521 |       }
522 |     }
523 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.IRFactory.TransformDispatcher.transformAsString(AstNode)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/IRFactory.java
Original range: 409-422
Documentation:
/**
     * Transforms the given node and then sets its type to Token.STRING if it
     * was Token.NAME. If its type was already Token.STRING, then quotes it.
     * Used for properties, as the old AST uses String tokens, while the new one
     * uses Name tokens for unquoted strings. For example, in
     * var o = {'a' : 1, b: 2};
     * the string 'a' is quoted, while the name b is turned into a string, but
     * unquoted.
     */
Method code:
409 |     private Node transformAsString(AstNode n) {
410 |       Node ret;
411 |       if (n instanceof Name) {
412 |         ret = transformNameAsString((Name)n);

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Compiler.parseInputs()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Compiler.java
Original range: 1240-1362

/**
   * Parses the externs and main inputs.
   *
   * @return A synthetic root node whose two children are the externs root
   *     and the main root
   */
Method code:
1240 |   Node parseInputs() {
1241 |     boolean devMode = options.devMode != DevMode.OFF;
1242 | 
1243 |     // If old roots exist (we are parsing a second time), detach each of the
1244 |     // individual file parse trees.
1245 |     if (externsRoot != null) {
1246 |       externsRoot.detachChildren();
1247 |     }
1248 |     if (jsRoot != null) {
1249 |       jsRoot.detachChildren();
1250 |     }
1251 | 
1252 |     // Parse main JS sources.
1253 |     jsRoot = IR.block();
1254 |     jsRoot.setIsSyntheticBlock(true);
1255 | 
1256 |     externsRoot = IR.block();
1257 |     externsRoot.setIsSyntheticBlock(true);
1258 | 
1259 |     externAndJsRoot = IR.block(externsRoot, jsRoot);
1260 |     externAndJsRoot.setIsSyntheticBlock(true);
1261 | 
1262 |     if (options.tracer.isOn()) {
1263 |       tracker = new PerformanceTracker(jsRoot, options.tracer);
1264 |       addChangeHandler(tracker.getCodeChangeHandler());
1265 |     }
1266 | 
1267 |     Tracer tracer = newTracer("parseInputs");
1268 | 
1269 |     try {
1270 |       // Parse externs sources.
1271 |       for (CompilerInput input : externs) {
1272 |         Node n = input.getAstRoot(this);
1273 |         if (hasErrors()) {
1274 |           return null;
1275 |         }
1276 |         externsRoot.addChildToBack(n);
1277 |       }
1278 | 
1279 |       // Modules inferred in ProcessCommonJS pass.
1280 |       if (options.transformAMDToCJSModules || options.processCommonJSModules) {
1281 |         processAMDAndCommonJSModules();
1282 |       }
1283 | 
1284 |       hoistExterns(externsRoot);
1285 | 
1286 |       // Check if the sources need to be re-ordered.
1287 |       boolean staleInputs = false;
1288 |       if (options.dependencyOptions.needsManagement()) {
1289 |         for (CompilerInput input : inputs) {
1290 |           // Forward-declare all the provided types, so that they
1291 |           // are not flagged even if they are dropped from the process.
1292 |           for (String provide : input.getProvides()) {
1293 |             getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(provide);
1294 |           }
1295 |         }
1296 | 
1297 |         try {
1298 |           inputs =
1299 |               (moduleGraph == null ? new JSModuleGraph(modules) : moduleGraph)
1300 |               .manageDependencies(options.dependencyOptions, inputs);
1301 |           staleInputs = true;
1302 |         } catch (CircularDependencyException e) {
1303 |           report(JSError.make(
1304 |               JSModule.CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY_ERROR, e.getMessage()));
1305 | 
1306 |           // If in IDE mode, we ignore the error and keep going.
1307 |           if (hasErrors()) {
1308 |             return null;
1309 |           }
1310 |         } catch (MissingProvideException e) {
1311 |           report(JSError.make(
1312 |               MISSING_ENTRY_ERROR, e.getMessage()));
1313 | 
1314 |           // If in IDE mode, we ignore the error and keep going.
1315 |           if (hasErrors()) {
1316 |             return null;
1317 |           }
1318 |         }
1319 |       }
1320 | 
1321 |       hoistNoCompileFiles();
1322 | 
1323 |       if (staleInputs) {
1324 |         repartitionInputs();
1325 |       }
1326 | 
1327 |       // Build the AST.
1328 |       for (CompilerInput input : inputs) {
1329 |         Node n = input.getAstRoot(this);
1330 |         if (n == null) {
1331 |           continue;
1332 |         }
1333 | 
1334 |         if (devMode) {
1335 |           runSanityCheck();
1336 |           if (hasErrors()) {
1337 |             return null;
1338 |           }
1339 |         }
1340 | 
1341 |         if (options.sourceMapOutputPath != null ||
1342 |             options.nameReferenceReportPath != null) {
1343 | 
1344 |           // Annotate the nodes in the tree with information from the
1345 |           // input file. This information is used to construct the SourceMap.
1346 |           SourceInformationAnnotator sia =
1347 |               new SourceInformationAnnotator(
1348 |                   input.getName(), options.devMode != DevMode.OFF);
1349 |           NodeTraversal.traverse(this, n, sia);
1350 |         }
1351 | 
1352 |         jsRoot.addChildToBack(n);
1353 |       }
1354 | 
1355 |       if (hasErrors()) {
1356 |         return null;
1357 |       }
1358 |       return externAndJsRoot;
1359 |     } finally {
1360 |       stopTracer(tracer, "parseInputs");
1361 |     }
1362 |   }

===== M0769 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeUtil.checkForStateChangeHelper(Node,boolean,AbstractCompiler)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java
Original range: 790-934
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns true if some node in n's subtree changes application state.
   * If {@code checkForNewObjects} is true, we assume that newly created
   * mutable objects (like object literals) change state. Otherwise, we assume
   * that they have no side effects.
   */
Method code:
790 |   private static boolean checkForStateChangeHelper(
791 |       Node n, boolean checkForNewObjects, AbstractCompiler compiler) {
792 |     // Rather than id which ops may have side effects, id the ones
793 |     // that we know to be safe
794 |     switch (n.getType()) {
795 |       // other side-effect free statements and expressions
796 |       case Token.AND:
797 |       case Token.BLOCK:
798 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
799 |       case Token.HOOK:
800 |       case Token.IF:
801 |       case Token.IN:
802 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
803 |       case Token.NUMBER:
804 |       case Token.OR:
805 |       case Token.THIS:
806 |       case Token.TRUE:
807 |       case Token.FALSE:
808 |       case Token.NULL:
809 |       case Token.STRING:
810 |       case Token.STRING_KEY:
811 |       case Token.SWITCH:
812 |       case Token.TRY:
813 |       case Token.EMPTY:
814 |         break;
815 | 
816 |       // Throws are by definition side effects
817 |       case Token.THROW:
818 |         return true;
819 | 
820 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
821 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
822 |           return true;
823 |         }
824 |         for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
825 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
826 |                   c.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
827 |             return true;
828 |           }
829 |         }
830 |         return false;
831 | 
832 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
833 |       case Token.REGEXP:
834 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
835 |           return true;
836 |         }
837 |         break;
838 | 
839 |       case Token.VAR:    // empty var statement (no declaration)
840 |       case Token.NAME:   // variable by itself
841 |         if (n.getFirstChild() != null) {
842 |           return true;
843 |         }
844 |         break;
845 | 
846 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
847 |         // Function expressions don't have side-effects, but function
848 |         // declarations change the namespace. Either way, we don't need to
849 |         // check the children, since they aren't executed at declaration time.
850 |         return checkForNewObjects || !isFunctionExpression(n);
851 | 
852 |       case Token.NEW:
853 |         if (checkForNewObjects) {
854 |           return true;
855 |         }
856 | 
857 |         if (!constructorCallHasSideEffects(n)) {
858 |           // loop below will see if the constructor parameters have
859 |           // side-effects
860 |           break;
861 |         }
862 |         return true;
863 | 
864 |       case Token.CALL:
865 |         // calls to functions that have no side effects have the no
866 |         // side effect property set.
867 |         if (!functionCallHasSideEffects(n, compiler)) {
868 |           // loop below will see if the function parameters have
869 |           // side-effects
870 |           break;
871 |         }
872 |         return true;
873 | 
874 |       default:
875 |         if (isSimpleOperatorType(n.getType())) {
876 |           break;
877 |         }
878 | 
879 |         if (isAssignmentOp(n)) {
880 |           Node assignTarget = n.getFirstChild();
881 |           if (assignTarget.isName()) {
882 |             return true;
883 |           }
884 | 
885 |           // Assignments will have side effects if
886 |           // a) The RHS has side effects, or
887 |           // b) The LHS has side effects, or
888 |           // c) A name on the LHS will exist beyond the life of this statement.
889 |           if (checkForStateChangeHelper(
890 |                   n.getFirstChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler) ||
891 |               checkForStateChangeHelper(
892 |                   n.getLastChild(), checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
893 |             return true;
894 |           }
895 | 
896 |           if (isGet(assignTarget)) {
897 |             // If the object being assigned to is a local object, don't
898 |             // consider this a side-effect as it can't be referenced
899 |             // elsewhere.  Don't do this recursively as the property might
900 |             // be an alias of another object, unlike a literal below.
901 |             Node current = assignTarget.getFirstChild();
902 |             if (evaluatesToLocalValue(current)) {
903 |               return false;
904 |             }
905 | 
906 |             // A literal value as defined by "isLiteralValue" is guaranteed
907 |             // not to be an alias, or any components which are aliases of
908 |             // other objects.
909 |             // If the root object is a literal don't consider this a
910 |             // side-effect.
911 |             while (isGet(current)) {
912 |               current = current.getFirstChild();
913 |             }
914 | 
915 |             return !isLiteralValue(current, true);
916 |           } else {
917 |             // TODO(johnlenz): remove this code and make this an exception. This
918 |             // is here only for legacy reasons, the AST is not valid but
919 |             // preserve existing behavior.
920 |             return !isLiteralValue(assignTarget, true);
921 |           }
922 |         }
923 | 
924 |         return true;
925 |     }
926 | 
927 |     for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
928 |       if (checkForStateChangeHelper(c, checkForNewObjects, compiler)) {
929 |         return true;
930 |       }
931 |     }
932 | 
933 |     return false;
934 |   }

===== M0774 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.FunctionTypeBuilder.getOrCreateConstructor()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/FunctionTypeBuilder.java
Original range: 659-695
Documentation:
/**
   * Returns a constructor function either by returning it from the
   * registry if it exists or creating and registering a new type. If
   * there is already a type, then warn if the existing type is
   * different than the one we are creating, though still return the
   * existing function if possible.  The primary purpose of this is
   * that registering a constructor will fail for all built-in types
   * that are initialized in {@link JSTypeRegistry}.  We a) want to
   * make sure that the type information specified in the externs file
   * matches what is in the registry and b) annotate the externs with
   * the {@link JSType} from the registry so that there are not two
   * separate JSType objects for one type.
   */
Method code:
659 |   private FunctionType getOrCreateConstructor() {
660 |     FunctionType fnType = typeRegistry.createConstructorType(
661 |         fnName, contents.getSourceNode(), parametersNode, returnType);
662 |     JSType existingType = typeRegistry.getType(fnName);
663 | 
664 |     if (existingType != null) {
665 |       boolean isInstanceObject = existingType.isInstanceType();
666 |       if (isInstanceObject || fnName.equals("Function")) {
667 |         FunctionType existingFn =
668 |             isInstanceObject ?
669 |             existingType.toObjectType().getConstructor() :
670 |             typeRegistry.getNativeFunctionType(FUNCTION_FUNCTION_TYPE);
671 | 
672 |         if (existingFn.getSource() == null) {
673 |           existingFn.setSource(contents.getSourceNode());
674 |         }
675 | 
676 |         if (!existingFn.hasEqualCallType(fnType)) {
677 |           reportWarning(TYPE_REDEFINITION, fnName,
678 |               fnType.toString(), existingFn.toString());
679 |         }
680 | 
681 |         return existingFn;
682 |       } else {
683 |         // We fall through and return the created type, even though it will fail
684 |         // to register. We have no choice as we have to return a function. We
685 |         // issue an error elsewhere though, so the user should fix it.
686 |       }
687 |     }
688 | 
689 |     maybeSetBaseType(fnType);
690 | 
691 |     if (getScopeDeclaredIn().isGlobal() && !fnName.isEmpty()) {
692 |       typeRegistry.declareType(fnName, fnType.getInstanceType());
693 |     }
694 |     return fnType;
695 |   }

/**
   * Visits an assignment <code>lvalue = rvalue</code>. If the
   * <code>lvalue</code> is a prototype modification, we change the schema
   * of the object type it is referring to.
   * @param t the traversal
   * @param assign the assign node

Method code:
839 |   private void visitAssign(NodeTraversal t, Node assign) {
840 |     JSDocInfo info = assign.getJSDocInfo();
841 |     Node lvalue = assign.getFirstChild();
842 |     Node rvalue = assign.getLastChild();
843 | 
844 |     // Check property sets to 'object.property' when 'object' is known.
845 |     if (lvalue.isGetProp()) {
846 |       Node object = lvalue.getFirstChild();
847 |       JSType objectJsType = getJSType(object);
848 |       String property = lvalue.getLastChild().getString();
849 | 
850 |       // the first name in this getprop refers to an interface
851 |       // we perform checks in addition to the ones below
852 |       if (object.isGetProp()) {

856 |           visitInterfaceGetprop(t, assign, object, property, lvalue, rvalue);
857 |         }
858 |       }
859 |

861 | 
862 |       // Prototype assignments are special, because they actually affect
863 |       // the definition of a class. These are mostly validated
864 |       // during TypedScopeCreator, and we only look for the "dumb" cases here.
865 |       // object.prototype = ...;
866 |       if (property.equals("prototype")) {
867 |         if (objectJsType != null && objectJsType.isFunctionType()) {
868 |           FunctionType functionType = objectJsType.toMaybeFunctionType();
869 |           if (functionType.isConstructor()) {
870 |             JSType rvalueType = rvalue.getJSType();
871 |             validator.expectObject(t, rvalue, rvalueType,
872 |                 OVERRIDING_PROTOTYPE_WITH_NON_OBJECT);
873 |             return;
874 |           }
875 |         }
876 |       }
877 | 
878 |       // The generic checks for 'object.property' when 'object' is known,
879 |       // and 'property' is declared on it.
880 |       // object.property = ...;
881 |       ObjectType type = ObjectType.cast(
882 |           objectJsType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined());
883 |       if (type != null) {
884 |         if (type.hasProperty(property) &&
885 |             !type.isPropertyTypeInferred(property) &&
886 |             !propertyIsImplicitCast(type, property)) {
887 |           JSType expectedType = type.getPropertyType(property);
888 |           if (!expectedType.isUnknownType()) {
889 |             validator.expectCanAssignToPropertyOf(

891 |                 expectedType, object, property);

894 |             return;
895 |           }
896 |         }

900 |       // lookups, then check inheritance anyway with the unknown type.
901 |       checkPropertyInheritanceOnGetpropAssign(
902 |           t, assign, object, property, info, getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE));
903 |     }
904 | 
905 |     // Check qualified name sets to 'object' and 'object.property'.
906 |     // This can sometimes handle cases when the type of 'object' is not known.
907 |     // e.g.,

928 |         }
929 |       }

933 |     Node rightChild = assign.getLastChild();

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.SourceFile.getLine(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/SourceFile.java
Original range: 215-248
Documentation:
/**
   * Gets the source line for the indicated line number.
   *
   * @param lineNumber the line number, 1 being the first line of the file.
   * @return The line indicated. Does not include the newline at the end
   *     of the file. Returns {@code null} if it does not exist,
   *     or if there was an IO exception.
   */
Method code:
215 |   public String getLine(int lineNumber) {
216 |     findLineOffsets();
217 |     if (lineNumber > lineOffsets.length) {
218 |       return null;
219 |     }
220 | 
221 |     if (lineNumber < 1) {
222 |       lineNumber = 1;
223 |     }
224 | 
225 |     int pos = lineOffsets[lineNumber - 1];
226 |     String js = "";
227 |     try {
228 |       // NOTE(nicksantos): Right now, this is optimized for few warnings.
229 |       // This is probably the right trade-off, but will be slow if there
230 |       // are lots of warnings in one file.
231 |       js = getCode();
232 |     } catch (IOException e) {
233 |       return null;
234 |     }
235 | 
236 |     if (js.indexOf('\n', pos) == -1) {
237 |       // If next new line cannot be found, there are two cases
238 |       // 1. pos already reaches the end of file, then null should be returned
239 |       // 2. otherwise, return the contents between pos and the end of file.
240 |       if (pos >= js.length()) {
241 |         return null;
242 |       } else {
243 |         return js.substring(pos, js.length());
244 |       }
245 |     } else {
246 |       return js.substring(pos, js.indexOf('\n', pos));
247 |     }
248 |   }

/**
   * Tells the type system that {@code owner} may have a property named
   * {@code propertyName}. This allows the registry to keep track of what
   * types a property is defined upon.
   *
   * This is NOT the same as saying that {@code owner} must have a property
   * named type. ObjectType#hasProperty attempts to minimize false positives
   * ("if we're not sure, then don't type check this property"). The type
   * registry, on the other hand, should attempt to minimize false negatives
   * ("if this property is assigned anywhere in the program, it must
   * show up in the type registry").

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.VarCheck.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/VarCheck.java
Original range: 120-203
Documentation:

Method code:
120 |   @Override
121 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
122 |     if (!n.isName()) {
123 |       return;
124 |     }
125 | 
126 |     String varName = n.getString();
127 | 
128 |     // Only a function can have an empty name.
129 |     if (varName.isEmpty()) {
130 |       Preconditions.checkState(parent.isFunction());
131 |       Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent));
132 |       return;
133 |     }
134 | 
135 |     // Check if this is a declaration for a var that has been declared
136 |     // elsewhere. If so, mark it as a duplicate.
137 |     if ((parent.isVar() ||
138 |          NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(parent)) &&
139 |         varsToDeclareInExterns.contains(varName)) {
140 |       createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
141 | 
142 |       n.addSuppression("duplicate");
143 |     }
144 | 
145 |     // Check that the var has been declared.
146 |     Scope scope = t.getScope();
147 |     Scope.Var var = scope.getVar(varName);
148 |     if (var == null) {
149 |       if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(parent)) {
150 |         // e.g. [ function foo() {} ], it's okay if "foo" isn't defined in the
151 |         // current scope.
152 |       } else {
153 |         // The extern checks are stricter, don't report a second error.
154 |         if (!strictExternCheck || !t.getInput().isExtern()) {
155 |           t.report(n, UNDEFINED_VAR_ERROR, varName);
156 |         }
157 | 
158 |         if (sanityCheck) {
159 |           throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected variable " + varName);
160 |         } else {
161 |           createSynthesizedExternVar(varName);
162 |           scope.getGlobalScope().declare(varName, n,
163 |               null, getSynthesizedExternsInput());
164 |         }
165 |       }
166 |       return;
167 |     }
168 | 
169 |     CompilerInput currInput = t.getInput();
170 |     CompilerInput varInput = var.input;
171 |     if (currInput == varInput || currInput == null || varInput == null) {
172 |       // The variable was defined in the same file. This is fine.
173 |       return;
174 |     }
175 | 
176 |     // Check module dependencies.
177 |     JSModule currModule = currInput.getModule();
178 |     JSModule varModule = varInput.getModule();
179 |     JSModuleGraph moduleGraph = compiler.getModuleGraph();
180 |     if (!sanityCheck &&
181 |         varModule != currModule && varModule != null && currModule != null) {
182 |       if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(currModule, varModule)) {
183 |         // The module dependency was properly declared.
184 |       } else {
185 |         if (scope.isGlobal()) {
186 |           if (moduleGraph.dependsOn(varModule, currModule)) {
187 |             // The variable reference violates a declared module dependency.
188 |             t.report(n, VIOLATED_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
189 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
190 |           } else {
191 |             // The variable reference is between two modules that have no
192 |             // dependency relationship. This should probably be considered an
193 |             // error, but just issue a warning for now.
194 |             t.report(n, MISSING_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
195 |                      currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
196 |           }
197 |         } else {
198 |           t.report(n, STRICT_MODULE_DEP_ERROR,
199 |                    currModule.getName(), varModule.getName(), varName);
200 |         }
201 |       }
202 |     }
203 |   }

804 |     @Override
805 |     Node processObjectLiteral(ObjectLiteral literalNode) {
806 |       if (literalNode.isDestructuring()) {
807 |         reportDestructuringAssign(literalNode);
808 |       }
809 | 
810 |       Node node = newNode(Token.OBJECTLIT);
811 |       for (ObjectProperty el : literalNode.getElements()) {
812 |         if (config.languageMode == LanguageMode.ECMASCRIPT3) {
813 |           if (el.isGetter()) {

836 |             reportSetterParam(el.getLeft());

===== M0880 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.branchedFlowThrough(Node,FlowScope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 134-246
Documentation:

Method code:
134 |   @Override
135 |   @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough")
136 |   List<FlowScope> branchedFlowThrough(Node source, FlowScope input) {
137 |     // NOTE(nicksantos): Right now, we just treat ON_EX edges like UNCOND
138 |     // edges. If we wanted to be perfect, we'd actually JOIN all the out
139 |     // lattices of this flow with the in lattice, and then make that the out
140 |     // lattice for the ON_EX edge. But it's probably to expensive to be
141 |     // worthwhile.
142 |     FlowScope output = flowThrough(source, input);
143 |     Node condition = null;
144 |     FlowScope conditionFlowScope = null;
145 |     BooleanOutcomePair conditionOutcomes = null;
146 | 
147 |     List<DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch>> branchEdges = getCfg().getOutEdges(source);
148 |     List<FlowScope> result = Lists.newArrayListWithCapacity(branchEdges.size());
149 |     for (DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch> branchEdge : branchEdges) {
150 |       Branch branch = branchEdge.getValue();
151 |       FlowScope newScope = output;
152 | 
153 |       switch (branch) {
154 |         case ON_TRUE:
155 |           if (NodeUtil.isForIn(source)) {
156 |             // item is assigned a property name, so its type should be string.
157 |             Node item = source.getFirstChild();
158 |             Node obj = item.getNext();
159 | 
160 |             FlowScope informed = traverse(obj, output.createChildFlowScope());
161 | 
162 |             if (item.isVar()) {
163 |               item = item.getFirstChild();
164 |             }
165 |             if (item.isName()) {
166 |               JSType iterKeyType = getNativeType(STRING_TYPE);
167 |               ObjectType objType = getJSType(obj).dereference();
168 |               JSType objIndexType = objType == null ?
169 |                   null : objType.getIndexType();
170 |               if (objIndexType != null && !objIndexType.isUnknownType()) {
171 |                 JSType narrowedKeyType =
172 |                     iterKeyType.getGreatestSubtype(objIndexType);
173 |                 if (!narrowedKeyType.isEmptyType()) {
174 |                   iterKeyType = narrowedKeyType;
175 |                 }
176 |               }
177 |               redeclareSimpleVar(informed, item, iterKeyType);
178 |             }
179 |             newScope = informed;
180 |             break;
181 |           }
182 | 
183 |           // FALL THROUGH
184 | 
185 |         case ON_FALSE:
186 |           if (condition == null) {
187 |             condition = NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(source);
188 |             if (condition == null && source.isCase()) {
189 |               condition = source;
190 | 
191 |               // conditionFlowScope is cached from previous iterations
192 |               // of the loop.
193 |               if (conditionFlowScope == null) {
194 |                 conditionFlowScope = traverse(
195 |                     condition.getFirstChild(), output.createChildFlowScope());
196 |               }
197 |             }
198 |           }
199 | 
200 |           if (condition != null) {
201 |             if (condition.isAnd() ||
202 |                 condition.isOr()) {
203 |               // When handling the short-circuiting binary operators,
204 |               // the outcome scope on true can be different than the outcome
205 |               // scope on false.
206 |               //
207 |               // TODO(nicksantos): The "right" way to do this is to
208 |               // carry the known outcome all the way through the
209 |               // recursive traversal, so that we can construct a
210 |               // different flow scope based on the outcome. However,
211 |               // this would require a bunch of code and a bunch of
212 |               // extra computation for an edge case. This seems to be
213 |               // a "good enough" approximation.
214 | 
215 |               // conditionOutcomes is cached from previous iterations
216 |               // of the loop.
217 |               if (conditionOutcomes == null) {
218 |                 conditionOutcomes = condition.isAnd() ?
219 |                     traverseAnd(condition, output.createChildFlowScope()) :
220 |                     traverseOr(condition, output.createChildFlowScope());
221 |               }
222 |               newScope =
223 |                   reverseInterpreter.getPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome(
224 |                       condition,
225 |                       conditionOutcomes.getOutcomeFlowScope(
226 |                           condition.getType(), branch == Branch.ON_TRUE),
227 |                       branch == Branch.ON_TRUE);
228 |             } else {
229 |               // conditionFlowScope is cached from previous iterations
230 |               // of the loop.
231 |               if (conditionFlowScope == null) {
232 |                 conditionFlowScope =
233 |                     traverse(condition, output.createChildFlowScope());
234 |               }
235 |               newScope =
236 |                   reverseInterpreter.getPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome(
237 |                       condition, conditionFlowScope, branch == Branch.ON_TRUE);
238 |             }
239 |           }
240 |           break;
241 |       }
242 | 
243 |       result.add(newScope.optimize());
244 |     }
245 |     return result;
246 |   }

Documentation:
/**
     * Replace the provide statement.
     *
     * If we're providing a name with no definition, then create one.
     * If we're providing a name with a duplicate definition, then make sure
     * that definition becomes a declaration.
     */
Method code:
890 |     void replace() {
891 |       if (firstNode == null) {
892 |         // Don't touch the base case ('goog').
893 |         replacementNode = candidateDefinition;
894 |         return;
895 |       }
896 | 
897 |       // Handle the case where there is a duplicate definition for an explicitly
898 |       // provided symbol.
899 |       if (candidateDefinition != null && explicitNode != null) {
900 |         explicitNode.detachFromParent();
901 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
902 | 
903 |         // Does this need a VAR keyword?
904 |         replacementNode = candidateDefinition;
905 |         if (candidateDefinition.isExprResult() &&
906 |             !candidateDefinition.getFirstChild().isQualifiedName()) {
907 |           candidateDefinition.putBooleanProp(Node.IS_NAMESPACE, true);
908 |           Node assignNode = candidateDefinition.getFirstChild();
909 |           Node nameNode = assignNode.getFirstChild();
910 |           if (nameNode.isName()) {
911 |             // Need to convert this assign to a var declaration.
912 |             Node valueNode = nameNode.getNext();
913 |             assignNode.removeChild(nameNode);
914 |             assignNode.removeChild(valueNode);
915 |             nameNode.addChildToFront(valueNode);
916 |             Node varNode = IR.var(nameNode);
917 |             varNode.copyInformationFrom(candidateDefinition);
918 |             candidateDefinition.getParent().replaceChild(
919 |                 candidateDefinition, varNode);
920 |             nameNode.setJSDocInfo(assignNode.getJSDocInfo());
921 |             compiler.reportCodeChange();
922 |             replacementNode = varNode;
923 |           }
924 |         }
925 |       } else {
926 |         // Handle the case where there's not a duplicate definition.
927 |         replacementNode = createDeclarationNode();
928 |         if (firstModule == minimumModule) {
929 |           firstNode.getParent().addChildBefore(replacementNode, firstNode);
930 |         } else {
931 |           // In this case, the name was implicitly provided by two independent
932 |           // modules. We need to move this code up to a common module.
933 |           int indexOfDot = namespace.lastIndexOf('.');
934 |           if (indexOfDot == -1) {
935 |             // Any old place is fine.
936 |             compiler.getNodeForCodeInsertion(minimumModule)
937 |                 .addChildToBack(replacementNode);
938 |           } else {
939 |             // Add it after the parent namespace.
940 |             ProvidedName parentName =
941 |                 providedNames.get(namespace.substring(0, indexOfDot));
942 |             Preconditions.checkNotNull(parentName);
943 |             Preconditions.checkNotNull(parentName.replacementNode);
944 |             parentName.replacementNode.getParent().addChildAfter(
945 |                 replacementNode, parentName.replacementNode);
946 |           }
947 |         }
948 |         if (explicitNode != null) {
949 |           explicitNode.detachFromParent();
950 |         }
951 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
952 |       }
953 |     }

175 |   @Override
176 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
177 |     switch (n.getType()) {
178 |       case Token.CALL:
179 |         boolean isExpr = parent.isExprResult();
180 |         Node left = n.getFirstChild();
181 |         if (left.isGetProp()) {
182 |           Node name = left.getFirstChild();
183 |           if (name.isName() &&
184 |               GOOG.equals(name.getString())) {
185 |             // For the sake of simplicity, we report code changes
186 |             // when we see a provides/requires, and don't worry about
187 |             // reporting the change when we actually do the replacement.
188 |             String methodName = name.getNext().getString();
189 |             if ("base".equals(methodName)) {
190 |               processBaseClassCall(t, n);
191 |             } else if (!isExpr) {
192 |               // All other methods must be called in an EXPR.
193 |               break;
194 |             } else if ("require".equals(methodName)) {
195 |               processRequireCall(t, n, parent);
196 |             } else if ("provide".equals(methodName)) {
197 |               processProvideCall(t, n, parent);
198 |             } else if ("exportSymbol".equals(methodName)) {
199 |               Node arg = left.getNext();
200 |               if (arg.isString()) {
201 |                 int dot = arg.getString().indexOf('.');
202 |                 if (dot == -1) {
203 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString());
204 |                 } else {
205 |                   exportedVariables.add(arg.getString().substring(0, dot));
206 |                 }
207 |               }
208 |             } else if ("addDependency".equals(methodName)) {
209 |               CodingConvention convention = compiler.getCodingConvention();
210 |               List<String> typeDecls =

212 |               if (typeDecls != null) {
213 |                 for (String typeDecl : typeDecls) {
214 |                   compiler.getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(typeDecl);
215 |                 }

219 |               // get compiled out.

221 |               compiler.reportCodeChange();
222 |             } else if ("setCssNameMapping".equals(methodName)) {
223 |               processSetCssNameMapping(t, n, parent);
224 |             }

230 |       case Token.NAME:
231 |         // If this is an assignment to a provided name, remove the provided
232 |         // object.
233 |         handleCandidateProvideDefinition(t, n, parent);
234 |         break;

237 |         handleTypedefDefinition(t, n, parent);

241 |         // If this is a declaration of a provided named function, this is an
242 |         // error. Hoisted functions will explode if they're provided.
243 |         if (t.inGlobalScope() &&

245 |           String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();

     * Move all the functions that are valid at the execution of the first
     * statement of the function to the beginning of the function definition.

640 |     private void moveNamedFunctions(Node functionBody) {
641 |       Preconditions.checkState(
642 |           functionBody.getParent().isFunction());

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 217-292
Documentation:

Method code:
217 |   @Override
218 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(
219 |       NodeTraversal nodeTraversal, Node n, Node parent) {
220 |     astPosition.put(n, astPositionCounter++);
221 | 
222 |     switch (n.getType()) {
223 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
224 |         if (shouldTraverseFunctions || n == cfg.getEntry().getValue()) {
225 |           exceptionHandler.push(n);
226 |           return true;
227 |         }
228 |         return false;
229 |       case Token.TRY:
230 |         exceptionHandler.push(n);
231 |         return true;
232 |     }
233 | 
234 |     /*
235 |      * We are going to stop the traversal depending on what the node's parent
236 |      * is.
237 |      *
238 |      * We are only interested in adding edges between nodes that change control
239 |      * flow. The most obvious ones are loops and IF-ELSE's. A statement
240 |      * transfers control to its next sibling.
241 |      *
242 |      * In case of an expression tree, there is no control flow within the tree
243 |      * even when there are short circuited operators and conditionals. When we
244 |      * are doing data flow analysis, we will simply synthesize lattices up the
245 |      * expression tree by finding the meet at each expression node.
246 |      *
247 |      * For example: within a Token.SWITCH, the expression in question does not
248 |      * change the control flow and need not to be considered.
249 |      */
250 |     if (parent != null) {
251 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
252 |         case Token.FOR:
253 |           // Only traverse the body of the for loop.
254 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
255 | 
256 |         // Skip the conditions.
257 |         case Token.IF:
258 |         case Token.WHILE:
259 |         case Token.WITH:
260 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
261 |         case Token.DO:
262 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
263 |         // Only traverse the body of the cases
264 |         case Token.SWITCH:
265 |         case Token.CASE:
266 |         case Token.CATCH:
267 |         case Token.LABEL:
268 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
269 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
270 |           return n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
271 |         case Token.CONTINUE:
272 |         case Token.BREAK:
273 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
274 |         case Token.VAR:
275 |         case Token.RETURN:
276 |         case Token.THROW:
277 |           return false;
278 |         case Token.TRY:
279 |           /* Just before we are about to visit the second child of the TRY node,
280 |            * we know that we will be visiting either the CATCH or the FINALLY.
281 |            * In other words, we know that the post order traversal of the TRY
282 |            * block has been finished, no more exceptions can be caught by the
283 |            * handler at this TRY block and should be taken out of the stack.
284 |            */
285 |           if (n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext()) {
286 |             Preconditions.checkState(exceptionHandler.peek() == parent);
287 |             exceptionHandler.pop();
288 |           }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 |     return true;
292 |   }

/**
   * Detects a cycle in the implicit prototype chain. This method accesses
   * the {@link #getImplicitPrototype()} method and must therefore be
   * invoked only after the object is sufficiently initialized to respond to
   * calls to this method.<p>

   * The method is not thread safe.<p>

/**
     * Updates our representation of the global namespace to reflect a read
     * of a global name's longest prefix before the "prototype" property if the
     * name includes the "prototype" property. Does nothing otherwise.
     *
     * @param t The current node traversal
     * @param n The node currently being visited
     * @param parent {@code n}'s parent
     * @param name The global name (e.g. "a" or "a.b.c.d")
     * @return Whether the name was handled
     */
Method code:
766 |     boolean maybeHandlePrototypePrefix(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent,
767 |         String name) {
768 |       // We use a string-based approach instead of inspecting the parse tree
769 |       // to avoid complexities with object literals, possibly nested, beneath
770 |       // assignments.
771 | 
772 |       int numLevelsToRemove;
773 |       String prefix;
774 |       if (name.endsWith(".prototype")) {
775 |         numLevelsToRemove = 1;
776 |         prefix = name.substring(0, name.length() - 10);
777 |       } else {
778 |         int i = name.indexOf(".prototype.");
779 |         if (i == -1) {
780 |           return false;
781 |         }
782 |         prefix = name.substring(0, i);
783 |         numLevelsToRemove = 2;
784 |         i = name.indexOf('.', i + 11);
785 |         while (i >= 0) {
786 |           numLevelsToRemove++;
787 |           i = name.indexOf('.', i + 1);
788 |         }
789 |       }
790 | 
791 |       if (parent != null && NodeUtil.isObjectLitKey(n, parent)) {
792 |         // Object literal keys have no prefix that's referenced directly per
793 |         // key, so we're done.
794 |         return true;
795 |       }
796 | 
797 |       for (int i = 0; i < numLevelsToRemove; i++) {
798 |         parent = n;
799 |         n = n.getFirstChild();
800 |       }
801 | 
802 |       handleGet(t, n, parent, prefix, Ref.Type.PROTOTYPE_GET);
803 |       return true;
804 |     }

610 |   @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
611 |   static <T> T runCallable(
612 |       final Callable<T> callable, boolean useLargeStackThread, boolean trace) {
613 | 
614 |     // Under JRE 1.6, the JS Compiler overflows the stack when running on some
615 |     // large or complex JS code. Here we start a new thread with a larger
616 |     // stack in order to let the compiler do its thing, without having to
617 |     // increase the stack size for *every* thread (which is what -Xss does).
618 |     // Might want to add thread pool support for clients that compile a lot.
619 | 
620 |     final boolean dumpTraceReport = trace;
621 |     final Object[] result = new Object[1];
622 |     final Throwable[] exception = new Throwable[1];
623 |     Runnable runnable = new Runnable() {
624 |       @Override
625 |       public void run() {
626 |         try {
627 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
628 |             Tracer.initCurrentThreadTrace();
629 |           }
630 |           result[0] = callable.call();
631 |         } catch (Throwable e) {
632 |           exception[0] = e;
633 |         } finally {
634 |           if (dumpTraceReport) {
635 |             Tracer.logAndClearCurrentThreadTrace();
636 |           }
637 |         }
638 |       }
639 |     };
640 | 
641 |     if (useLargeStackThread) {
642 |       Thread th = new Thread(null, runnable, "jscompiler", COMPILER_STACK_SIZE);
643 |       th.start();
644 |       while (true) {
645 |         try {
646 |           th.join();
647 |           break;
648 |         } catch (InterruptedException ignore) {
649 |           // ignore
650 |         }
651 |       }
652 |     } else {
653 |       runnable.run();
654 |     }
655 | 
656 |     // Pass on any exception caught by the runnable object.
657 |     if (exception[0] != null) {
658 |       throw new RuntimeException(exception[0]);
659 |     }
660 | 
661 |     return (T) result[0];

190 |     public static boolean isJSIdentifier(String s) {
191 |       int length = s.length();
192 | 
193 |       if (length == 0 || !Character.isJavaIdentifierStart(s.charAt(0)))
194 |         return false;
195 | 
196 |       for (int i = 1; i < length; i++) {
197 |         if (!Character.isJavaIdentifierPart(s.charAt(i))) {
198 |           return false;
199 |         }
200 |       }

===== M0952 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ClosureOptimizePrimitives.processObjectCreateCalls(List<Node>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ClosureOptimizePrimitives.java
Original range: 75-100
Documentation:
/**
   * Converts all of the given call nodes to object literals that are safe to
   * do so.
   */
Method code:
75 |   private void processObjectCreateCalls(List<Node> callNodes) {
76 |     for (Node callNode : callNodes) {
77 |       Node curParam = callNode.getFirstChild().getNext();
78 |       if (canOptimizeObjectCreate(curParam)) {
79 |         Node objNode = IR.objectlit().srcref(callNode);
80 |         while (curParam != null) {
81 |           Node keyNode = curParam;
82 |           Node valueNode = curParam.getNext();
83 |           curParam = valueNode.getNext();
84 | 
85 |           callNode.removeChild(keyNode);
86 |           callNode.removeChild(valueNode);
87 | 
88 |           if (!keyNode.isString()) {
89 |             keyNode = IR.string(NodeUtil.getStringValue(keyNode))
90 |                 .srcref(keyNode);
91 |           }
92 |           keyNode.setType(Token.STRING_KEY);
93 |           keyNode.setQuotedString();
94 |           objNode.addChildToBack(IR.propdef(keyNode, valueNode));
95 |         }
96 |         callNode.getParent().replaceChild(callNode, objNode);
97 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
98 |       }
99 |     }
100 |   }

286 |     @Override
287 |     public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
288 |       RefInfo refInfo = allRefInfo.get(n);
289 |       if (refInfo != null) {
290 |         Ref ref = refInfo.ref;
291 |         Name name = refInfo.name;
292 |         String fullName = name.getFullName();
293 |         switch (ref.type) {
294 |           case SET_FROM_GLOBAL:
295 |           case SET_FROM_LOCAL:
296 |             Node valParent = getValueParent(ref);
297 |             Node val = valParent.getLastChild();
298 |             if (valParent.isAssign() && name.isSimpleName() &&
299 |                 name.getDeclaration() == ref) {
300 |               // For defines, it's an error if a simple name is assigned
301 |               // before it's declared
302 |               compiler.report(
303 |                   t.makeError(val, INVALID_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, fullName));
304 |             } else if (processDefineAssignment(t, fullName, val, valParent)) {
305 |               // remove the assignment so that the variable is still declared,
306 |               // but no longer assigned to a value, e.g.,
307 |               // DEF_FOO = 5; // becomes "5;"
308 | 
309 |               // We can't remove the ASSIGN/VAR when we're still visiting its
310 |               // children, so we'll have to come back later to remove it.
311 |               refInfo.name.removeRef(ref);
312 |               lvalueToRemoveLater = valParent;
313 |             }
314 |             break;
315 |           default:
316 |             if (t.inGlobalScope()) {
317 |               // Treat this as a reference to a define in the global scope.
318 |               // After this point, the define must not be reassigned,
319 |               // or it's an error.
320 |               DefineInfo info = assignableDefines.get(fullName);
321 |               if (info != null) {
322 |                 setDefineInfoNotAssignable(info, t);
323 |                 assignableDefines.remove(fullName);
324 |               }
325 |             }
326 |             break;
327 |         }
328 |       }
329 |

331 |           n.getJSDocInfo() != null && n.getJSDocInfo().isDefine()) {
332 |         // warn about @define annotations in local scopes
333 |         compiler.report(
334 |             t.makeError(n, NON_GLOBAL_DEFINE_INIT_ERROR, ""));
335 |       }
336 | 
337 |       if (lvalueToRemoveLater == n) {
338 |         lvalueToRemoveLater = null;
339 |         if (n.isAssign()) {
340 |           Node last = n.getLastChild();
341 |           n.removeChild(last);
342 |           parent.replaceChild(n, last);
343 |         } else {
344 |           Preconditions.checkState(n.isName());
345 |           n.removeChild(n.getFirstChild());
346 |         }
347 |         compiler.reportCodeChange();
348 |       }

352 |           // If there's a function call in the global scope,
353 |           // we just say it's unsafe and freeze all the defines.
354 |           //
355 |           // NOTE(nicksantos): We could be a lot smarter here. For example,
356 |           // ReplaceOverriddenVars keeps a call graph of all functions and
357 |           // which functions/variables that they reference, and tries
358 |           // to statically determine which functions are "safe" and which

626 |     @Override
627 |     Node processFunctionNode(FunctionNode functionNode) {
628 |       Name name = functionNode.getFunctionName();
629 |       Boolean isUnnamedFunction = false;
630 |       if (name == null) {
631 |         int functionType = functionNode.getFunctionType();
632 |         if (functionType != FunctionNode.FUNCTION_EXPRESSION) {
633 |           errorReporter.error(
634 |             "unnamed function statement",
635 |             sourceName,
636 |             functionNode.getLineno(), "", 0);
637 | 
638 |           // Return the bare minimum to put the AST in a valid state.
639 |           return newNode(Token.EXPR_RESULT, Node.newNumber(0));
640 |         }
641 |         name = new Name();
642 |         name.setIdentifier("");
643 |         isUnnamedFunction = true;
644 |       }
645 |       Node node = newNode(Token.FUNCTION);
646 |       Node newName = transform(name);
647 |       if (isUnnamedFunction) {
648 |         // Old Rhino tagged the empty name node with the line number of the
649 |         // declaration.
650 |         newName.setLineno(functionNode.getLineno());
651 |         // TODO(bowdidge) Mark line number of paren correctly.
652 |         // Same problem as below - the left paren might not be on the
653 |         // same line as the function keyword.
654 |         int lpColumn = functionNode.getAbsolutePosition() +

662 |       // The left paren's complicated because it's not represented by an
663 |       // AstNode, so there's nothing that has the actual line number that it
664 |       // appeared on.  We know the paren has to appear on the same line as the
665 |       // function name (or else a semicolon will be inserted.)  If there's no
666 |       // function name, assume the paren was on the same line as the function.
667 |       // TODO(bowdidge): Mark line number of paren correctly.
668 |       Name fnName = functionNode.getFunctionName();
669 |       if (fnName != null) {
670 |         lp.setLineno(fnName.getLineno());
671 |       } else {
672 |         lp.setLineno(functionNode.getLineno());
673 |       }
674 |       int lparenCharno = functionNode.getLp() +
675 |           functionNode.getAbsolutePosition();
676 | 
677 |       lp.setCharno(position2charno(lparenCharno));
678 |       for (AstNode param : functionNode.getParams()) {
679 |         Node paramNode = transform(param);
680 |         // When in ideMode Rhino can generate a param list with only a single
681 |         // ErrorNode. This is transformed into an EMPTY node. Drop this node in
682 |         // ideMode to keep the AST in a valid state.
683 |         if (paramNode.isName()) {
684 |           lp.addChildToBack(paramNode);
685 |         } else {

687 |           // destructuring parameter assignments which aren't supported
688 |           // (an error has already been reported).
689 |           Preconditions.checkState(

693 |         }
694 |       }

696 |

Method code:
345 |   void setPrototypeBasedOn(ObjectType baseType, Node propertyNode) {
346 |     // This is a bit weird. We need to successfully handle these
347 |     // two cases:
348 |     // Foo.prototype = new Bar();
349 |     // and
350 |     // Foo.prototype = {baz: 3};
351 |     // In the first case, we do not want new properties to get
352 |     // added to Bar. In the second case, we do want new properties
353 |     // to get added to the type of the anonymous object.
354 |     //
355 |     // We handle this by breaking it into two cases:
356 |     //
357 |     // In the first case, we create a new PrototypeObjectType and set
358 |     // its implicit prototype to the type being assigned. This ensures
359 |     // that Bar will not get any properties of Foo.prototype, but properties
360 |     // later assigned to Bar will get inherited properly.
361 |     //
362 |     // In the second case, we just use the anonymous object as the prototype.
363 |     if (baseType.hasReferenceName() ||
364 |         isNativeObjectType() ||
365 |         baseType.isFunctionPrototypeType()) {
366 | 
367 |       baseType = new PrototypeObjectType(
368 |           registry, this.getReferenceName() + ".prototype", baseType);
369 |     }
370 |     setPrototype(baseType, propertyNode);
371 |   }

1114 |           safeResolve(prototypeSlot.getType(), t, scope));
1115 |     }
1116 |

1118 |     // is handled further upstream.
1119 |     //
1120 |     // TODO(nicksantos): Handle this correctly if we have a UnionType.
1121 |     //
1122 |     // TODO(nicksantos): In ES3, the run-time coerces "null" to the global
1123 |     // activation object. In ES5, it leaves it as null. Just punt on this
1124 |     // issue for now by coercing out null. This is complicated by the
1125 |     // fact that when most people write @this {Foo}, they really don't
1126 |     // mean "nullable Foo". For certain tags (like @extends) we de-nullify
1127 |     // the name for them.
1128 |     JSType maybeTypeOfThis = safeResolve(typeOfThis, t, scope);
1129 |     if (maybeTypeOfThis != null) {
1130 |       maybeTypeOfThis = maybeTypeOfThis.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
1131 |     }
1132 |     if (maybeTypeOfThis instanceof ObjectType) {
1133 |       typeOfThis = (ObjectType) maybeTypeOfThis;
1134 |     }
1135 | 
1136 |     boolean changed = false;
1137 |     ImmutableList.Builder<ObjectType> resolvedInterfaces =
1138 |         ImmutableList.builder();
1139 |     for (ObjectType iface : implementedInterfaces) {
1140 |       ObjectType resolvedIface = (ObjectType) iface.resolve(t, scope);
1141 |       resolvedInterfaces.add(resolvedIface);
1142 |       changed |= (resolvedIface != iface);
1143 |     }
1144 |     if (changed) {
1145 |       implementedInterfaces = resolvedInterfaces.build();
1146 |     }
1147 | 
1148 |     if (subTypes != null) {
1149 |       for (int i = 0; i < subTypes.size(); i++) {
1150 |         subTypes.set(
1151 |             i, JSType.toMaybeFunctionType(subTypes.get(i).resolve(t, scope)));
1152 |       }
1153 |     }
1154 | 
1155 |     return super.resolveInternal(t, scope);
1156 |   }

/**
     * Parse the directives, encode them in the AST, and remove their nodes.
     *
     * For information on ES5 directives, see section 14.1 of
     * ECMA-262, Edition 5.
     *
     * It would be nice if Rhino would eventually take care of this for
     * us, but right now their directive-processing is a one-off.
     */
Method code:
470 |     private void parseDirectives(Node node) {
471 |       // Remove all the directives, and encode them in the AST.

474 |         String directive = node.removeFirstChild().getFirstChild().getString();
475 |         if (directives == null) {

478 |           directives.add(directive);
479 |         }
480 |       }
481 |

483 |         node.setDirectives(directives);
484 |       }
485 |     }

1367 |   private void hoistExterns(Node externsRoot) {
1368 |     boolean staleInputs = false;

1371 |           options.closurePass) {
